jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Forward Deployed Engineering- Applied AI
jobs.description:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

Team Bio:

ServiceNow’s Applied AI Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team is where bold ideas meet transformative action. We partner with our most strategic customers to shape the future of enterprise AI. Together, we identify high-value opportunities, accelerate business outcomes, and build reusable AI-native solutions that advance the Now AI Platform.

Our mission: We partner deeply with our customers to build intelligent, scalable AI solutions that solve their most mission-critical challenges. By embedding in real-world complexity, we deliver fast, iterate with purpose, and transform every success into reusable patterns that accelerate transformation across the Now Platform and the broader enterprise.

Why This Role Matters

Enterprise leaders aren’t just experimenting with AI—they’re demanding outcomes. The next wave of adoption will be led by those who can move fast, deliver measurable value, and transform 1-off wins into repeatable success.

As a FDE Technical Program Manager, you operate on the frontlines of transformation. You will support ServiceNow’s cross-functional Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) teams in building and delivering intelligent, scalable AI solutions that solve our customers’ most mission-critical challenges.

You'll work in a fast-paced environment as our FDE team partners with key strategic customers to accelerate time to value. You will provide a proactive, strategic perspective, manage customer relationships, and drive tactical execution from initial conception through FDE build development, delivery, and successful completion.

Who You Are

You are a dynamic and innovative problem-solver who thrives in complex, fast-paced environments. You have a strong analytical mindset while still keeping focus on the bigger picture. You have a background managing SDLC processes while keeping a customer-first mentality. You have a passion for AI and scaling innovation. You excel at transforming ambiguity into clarity and have hands on experience driving projects/programs end to end.

What You’ll Do

Work seamlessly with software engineers, product managers, product designers, and customers, to deliver intelligent systems that address mission-critical challenges using AI.
Collaborate directly with customers to co-innovate AI solutions tailored to their needs, acting as the first point of contact or escalation.
Develop trusted relationships with key internal and external technology leaders and stakeholders to drive focus on the strategic build objectives and optimize build delivery - this includes supporting and holding resources accountable for their responsibilities within the build.
Drive large scale, cross-functional, high visibility AI software development builds on condensed timelines.
Organize complex, ambiguous problems into prioritized milestones, deliverables, and success criteria for your builds, translating business objectives into execution strategy (tactical and strategic).
Anticipate and remove obstacles that slow down or prevent builds from delivering on objectives, especially on the AI/ML deployment front.
Help manage risks, dependencies and escalate impediments, as well as releases and navigating AI release requirements.
Drive process improvements and create documentation to promote best practices using automation to replace repeatable, operational tasks.
Coordinate day to day activities required to deliver a great solution on time, as well as create transparency through reports, dashboards, and status updates.
Seek to continuously grow by proactively seeking and embracing constructive feedback, as well as provide feedback to colleagues to encourage an open and collaborative culture .

Qualifications

10+ years of project/program management experience in mid/large size software development companies.
A solid understanding of SDLC and release management practices in cloud-based SaSS or AI product organizations.
Prior work delivering AI or intelligent workflow solutions at scale, with proven success in deploying AI solutions that delivered tangible customer impact.
Familiarity with AI governance, compliance, and enterprise security practices
This role includes occasional travel (10-15%)

Preferred Qualifications

Demonstrated competence in key AI/ML software engineering program management best practices: program planning, schedule construction and management; risk assessment & mitigation, dependency management, change management, and predictive metrics.
Outstanding collaboration and communication skills - clearly communicate changes, requests, and deadlines to the teams and risks, status, progress, and decisions to a variety of audiences including executives.
Passion for working with people in technical and innovative environments, with the ability to work well with many different types of personalities in various functions.
Strong leadership and relationship building skills to influence and motivate without authority - masterful in the art of bringing people together.
Strong facilitation skills to lead/drive a variety of build events, with a high regard for quality, drive for continuous improvement across the organization, and ability to keep the big picture in view.
Experience deploying AI solutions to production and skilled at identifying waste/delays in AI end-to-end development, deployment, and release processes.
Exceptional team building and team management skills, including interpersonal skills, conflict resolution, and negotiation.
Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving.

For positions in this location, we offer a base pay of $171,900 - $300,800

jobs.title: Senior Photonic Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
PsiQuantum’s mission is to build the first useful quantum computers—machines capable of delivering the breakthroughs the field has long promised. Since our founding in 2016, our singular focus has been to build and deploy million-qubit, fault-tolerant quantum systems.

Quantum computers harness the laws of quantum mechanics to solve problems that even the most advanced supercomputers or AI systems will never reach. Their impact will span energy, pharmaceuticals, finance, agriculture, transportation, materials, and other foundational industries.

Our architecture and approach is based on silicon photonics. By leveraging the advanced semiconductor manufacturing industry—including partners like GlobalFoundries—we use the same high-volume processes that already produce billions of chips for telecom and consumer electronics. Photonics offers natural advantages for scale: photons don’t feel heat, are immune to electromagnetic interference, and integrate with existing cryogenic cooling and standard fiber-optic infrastructure.

In 2024, PsiQuantum announced government-funded projects to support the build-out of our first utility-scale quantum computers in Brisbane, Australia, and Chicago, Illinois. These initiatives reflect a growing recognition that quantum computing will be strategically and economically defining—and that now is the time to scale.

PsiQuantum also develops the algorithms and software needed to make these systems commercially valuable. Our application, software, and industry teams work directly with leading Fortune 500 companies—including Lockheed Martin, Mercedes-Benz, Boehringer Ingelheim, and Mitsubishi Chemical—to prepare quantum solutions for real-world impact.

Quantum computing is not an extension of classical computing. It represents a fundamental shift—and a path to mastering challenges that cannot be solved any other way. The potential is enormous, and we have a clear path to make it real.

Come join us.

Job Summary

Quantum computing promises to solve many important problems that could never be solved on any conventional computer. At PsiQuantum, we’re building a general purpose silicon photonic quantum computer to tackle these very problems. We are seeking an experienced and highly motivated Sr.
Photonic Technical Program Manager
to lead the planning, execution, and delivery of complex photonic integrated circuit (PIC) programs supporting our linear optical quantum computer (LOQC).

In this role, you will drive cross-functional alignment across design, test, systems, and manufacturing teams to ensure successful integration and performance of advanced photonic circuits and subsystems. You will be responsible for defining program milestones, managing dependencies, mitigating risks, and ensuring that silicon photonic technologies meet system-level requirements. As a central coordinator, you will translate technical challenges into actionable plans, enable data-driven decision-making, and ensure timely delivery of high-quality hardware.

This role requires a strong technical foundation in photonics combined with exceptional program management skills. You will play a key role in orchestrating multidisciplinary efforts, improving development processes, and scaling photonic hardware from development through pilot production.

Responsibilities

Lead end-to-end program management for silicon photonic circuit and subsystem development, from concept through pilot ramp
Drive cross-functional coordination between design, test, systems, and manufacturing teams to meet program objectives
Define program scope, schedules, milestones, and deliverables; track progress and manage risks and dependencies
Ensure alignment of performance requirements, test methodology, and calibration approaches across hardware levels
Facilitate data-driven decision-making by coordinating analysis of performance metrics and yield vs SA and system-level data
Support root-cause analysis, quality evaluations, and continuous improvements across development stages
Drive PIC and subassembly specifications and improvements in product performance and yield during the pilot ramp
Communicate program status, risks, and key insights to stakeholders and leadership

Experience/Qualifications

MS degree + 8+ years’ experience, or PhD + 5+ years’ experience in Electrical Engineering, Photonics, Physics, or related field
Strong understanding of silicon photonics, including active and passive devices, integration challenges, and manufacturing considerations
Experience working across multiple hardware development stages (R&D, prototyping, pilot production)
Strong analytical skills with ability to interpret complex data (JMP, Python, etc)
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with ability to align diverse teams
Highly organized, proactive, and able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment

Role Summary

Help build Amazon's next-generation field application for EV charger commissioning, troubleshooting, and preventative maintenance across the AMZL fleet. Program delivery: Plan and execute UAT across three release increments (Commissioning, Troubleshooting, Preventative Maintenance): scope, test plans, pilot-site selection, participant onboarding, feedback and defect loops, and release go/no-go criteria.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Cybersecurity, Metrics and Reporting
jobs.description:
At Solventum, we improve lives by helping healthcare professionals do their best work. Join a team using innovation and insight to make a real impact on the future of healthcare. All roles listed are with Solventum, and we’re committed to protecting your personal information—learn more in our Privacy Policy

Job Description

3M Health Care is now Solventum

At Solventum, we enable better, smarter, safer healthcare to improve lives. As a new company with a long legacy of creating breakthrough solutions for our customers’ toughest challenges, we pioneer game-changing innovations at the intersection of health, material and data science that change patients' lives for the better while enabling healthcare professionals to perform at their best. Because people, and their wellbeing, are at the heart of every scientific advancement we pursue.

We partner closely with the brightest minds in healthcare to ensure that every solution we create melds the latest technology with compassion and empathy. Because at Solventum, we never stop solving for you.

The Impact You’ll Make in this Role

As The Program Manager, Cybersecurity, Metrics And Reporting, You Will Have The Opportunity To Tap Into Your Curiosity And Collaborate With Some Of The Most Innovative And Diverse People Around The World. Here, You Will Make An Impact By

Cybersecurity Metrics and Reporting Strategy

Defining, implementing, and continuously evolving the cybersecurity metrics, reporting, and analytics strategy in alignment with organizational objectives and cyber risk priorities.
Serving as the cybersecurity strategy owner for metrics and reporting, translating data-driven analysis into strategic insights and recommendations for senior leadership.
Advancing cybersecurity measurement from operational activity metrics to risk-based and outcome-focused measures of control effectiveness, program performance, and resilience.
Influencing cybersecurity strategy, risk prioritization, and enterprise risk management decisions through analytics and performance reporting.
Establishing reporting maturity roadmaps and continuous improvement programs that advance cybersecurity measurement capabilities.

Metrics Governance and Standards

Establishing and governing cybersecurity KPIs, KRIs, performance measures, scorecards, and reporting standards.
Defining and maintaining metric definitions, methodologies, thresholds, ownership, and reporting requirements aligned with cybersecurity measurement priorities.
Maintaining a cybersecurity metrics inventory and reporting catalog that document approved measures, data sources, and intended audiences.
Ensuring consistent interpretation and use of cybersecurity metrics across dashboards, executive reporting, and materials used for board reporting.
Establishing lifecycle management and reporting controls for the introduction, review, change, and retirement of metrics and reporting artifacts.

Data Quality and Reporting Integrity

Defining data quality standards and overseeing controls that ensure the consistency, completeness, accuracy, and reliability of cybersecurity reporting data.
Holding data and implementation owners accountable for investigating and resolving data quality issues affecting cybersecurity metrics and reporting.
Partnering with data owners, system owners, and cybersecurity teams to validate data sources, reporting assumptions, and implementation accuracy.
Establishing validation, reconciliation, and quality review processes for cybersecurity reporting, including materials used for executive and board reporting.
Requiring traceability and transparency of metric calculations, data lineage, and reporting methodologies to support reliable interpretation and review.

Executive Reporting and Analytics

Leading the development and delivery of executive dashboards, scorecards, and cybersecurity reporting packages, including metrics and reporting used for the board.
Synthesizing complex cybersecurity, risk, and performance information into concise business insights and leadership communications.
Analyzing performance trends, risk indicators, and control effectiveness to identify emerging concerns, improvement opportunities, and recommended mitigation priorities.
Partnering with cybersecurity leadership to communicate cyber risk, program effectiveness, operational performance, and resilience to executive stakeholders and support board reporting.
Prioritizing concurrent reporting, analytics, and strategic initiatives while meeting established deadlines and enabling informed decision-making.

Technical Solutions, Automation, and Data Engineering

Setting the technical direction and requirements for cybersecurity reporting, analytics, and data integration solutions; overseeing implementation by delivery teams and platform owners.
Evaluating proposed queries, datasets, data models, and reporting logic to assess feasibility, accuracy, scalability, and alignment with approved metric definitions.
Leading initiatives to automate reporting and improve dashboards, scorecards, data visualization, and data pipelines without requiring hands-on development.
Assessing API, system integration, and automation approaches, challenging unsupported claims and requiring evidence that implementation meets reporting requirements.
Guiding the integration and governance of cybersecurity telemetry from security platforms, cloud environments, and identity systems to support reliable reporting and analytics.
Establishing implementation acceptance criteria and reviewing technical designs, validation results, and delivery evidence with development and platform teams.
Directing resolution of reporting discrepancies and integration challenges, ensuring technical explanations are accurate and corrective actions address underlying issues.
Evaluating opportunities for predictive analytics, risk forecasting, telemetry-driven automation, and AI-enabled analytics, and prioritizing adoption based on reporting needs and data readiness.

Cross-Functional Leadership and Partnership

Serving as the strategic advisor and accountable owner for cybersecurity measurement, reporting, and analytics priorities.
Aligning Cybersecurity, Technology, Risk Management, Audit, Compliance, and business stakeholders around cybersecurity measurement priorities.
Leading cross-functional programs and initiatives to define reporting requirements, resolve competing priorities, and advance the measurement roadmap.
Supporting audit and compliance activities with consistent cybersecurity reporting and traceable measurement evidence.
Representing the Metrics & Reporting function in governance forums, working groups, and strategic initiatives.

Leadership and Functional Support

Leading the Metrics & Reporting function through strategic ownership, program leadership, and influence, initially without direct reports.
Owning strategic planning and continuous improvement initiatives for cybersecurity metrics, analytics, and reporting.
Providing functional guidance and mentoring contributors on reporting practices, measurement methodologies, and data-driven decision-making.
Assuming people management responsibilities if and when the organizational structure evolves to support a team; timing will depend on organizational needs and other dependencies.

Your Skills And Expertise

To set you up for success in this role from day one, Solventum requires, at a minimum, the following qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Systems, Data Analytics, Computer Science, Engineering, Business Analytics, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
Minimum 10 years of experience in information technology, cybersecurity, or product security.
Minimum 8 years of experience in cybersecurity, technology risk, business intelligence, data analytics, or performance reporting.

AND

In addition to the above requirements, the following are also required:

Experience developing and governing cybersecurity metrics, KPIs, KRIs, and performance measurement frameworks.
Experience delivering executive reporting or reporting used by boards to support strategic decision-making.
Leadership experience managing programs or enterprise initiatives and guiding cross-functional stakeholders; prior direct people management is not required.
Technical fluency in reporting platforms, data models, SQL and query logic, APIs, and data integrations sufficient to assess implementation approaches, identify inaccurate technical claims, and validate delivery quality; hands-on development is not required.
Strong analytical and quantitative reasoning, with the ability to translate complex cybersecurity and performance data into concise executive communications.
Experience with cybersecurity technologies, controls, and governance, and the ability to prioritize concurrent reporting, analytics, and strategic initiatives.

Additional qualifications that could help you succeed even further in this role include:

Experience with Power BI, Tableau, ServiceNow, Archer, or equivalent data visualization and reporting platforms.
CISSP, CRISC, CISM, Security+, Certified Data Analyst, or equivalent certification.
Experience overseeing automated reporting, data integrations, or analytics delivery across multiple technology platforms.
Experience establishing cybersecurity reporting maturity roadmaps and advancing enterprise measurement capabilities.
Experience evaluating data modeling, dashboard design, and data visualization approaches for executive audiences.
Familiarity with cloud data platforms, cybersecurity telemetry, predictive analytics, or AI-enabled analytics.
Knowledge of NIST CSF, CIS Controls, ISO 27001, or NIST 800-53.

What we offer

Impact - The work you do here matters to millions.
Growth - Philadelphia is growing, why not grow with it?
Diversity & Inclusion - Find a career in a place where everyone belongs.
Benefits - We care about your well-being.

Agency Description

 The Office of Emergency Management (OEM) works to mitigate, plan, and prepare for emergencies; educate the public about preparedness; coordinate emergency response and recovery efforts; and develop tools and identify resources to support the overall preparedness of the City of Philadelphia. 

Job Description

Position Summary 

OEM is seeking a Homeland Security Program Manager. Candidates for this position should possess a strong desire to work in a team-oriented, fast-paced, professional public safety environment, and a willingness to serve the public in the sixth largest city in the nation. The successful candidate for this position will assist with the development, strategic planning, implementation, and evaluation of an integrated public safety preparedness program to support the preparedness for and response to emergency incidents in Philadelphia.

All personnel must be City residents within six months of hire and are required to serve periodically on on-call field response teams. OEM staff also periodically work during non-business hours for extended periods of time, as needed in a field environment, and during activations of Philadelphia’s Emergency Operations Center (EOC).

Essential Functions 

Homeland security planning is a critical component of public safety operations. The Homeland Security Program Manager, under the direction of the First Deputy Director, is responsible for a range of activities including, but not limited to, the following:

Develop, maintain, and upon activation, implement emergency management and homeland security plans, protocols, and policies that improve coordination, situational awareness, and overall readiness.
Work with federal, state, regional, and local partners on preparedness efforts, threat and hazard discussions, information sharing, and capability development.
Support planning and analysis related to critical infrastructure security, operational coordination, public information, and situational assessment.
Coordinate interagency planning and public safety event action plan development for major or significant events to ensure consistent procedures and clear communication.
Manage and contribute to the Special Event Assessment Rating (SEAR) data‑call process, gathering, organizing, and submitting relevant information from OEM and partner agencies.
Support the annual Threat & Hazard Identification Risk Assessment (THIR) process, including collecting capability data, identifying gaps, and completing required documentation.
Develop and deliver training based on agency plans and procedures to strengthen operational readiness and address identified gaps.
Assist with planning, conducting, and evaluating exercises that test capabilities and address priority threats and hazards.
Build and maintain partnerships with government agencies, community organizations, non‑profits, and private‑sector partners to support preparedness and resilience.
Complete training required to maintain proficiency in emergency management and homeland security planning and coordination.
Conduct special projects related to homeland security or emergency management priorities.
Manage two staff positions supporting the portfolio.
Perform other duties as needed to support OEM.

Competencies 

Strong interpersonal skills 
Effective oral and written communication skills 
Strong leadership and negotiation skills 
Professional conduct and accountability 
Proven time-management skills 
Ability to maintain confidentiality and to establish a “need to know” with partners 

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities 

Ability to work independently. 
Ability to multitask effectively.  
Ability to maintain effective working relationships and develop partnerships. 
Ability to coordinate diverse groups toward a common goal. 
Ability to complete tasks and projects in a timely manner. 
Ability to contribute and coordinate work in a team. 
Ability to interpret federal and state emergency management requirements and regulations. 
Proficiency with Microsoft Office software (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Access, Outlook) and ability to use other web-based platforms for information collection and submission. 

Qualifications

 Education and Experience 

Completion of a bachelor’s degree in a related field from an accredited college;
Experience working within an emergency management or other public safety organization is preferred. 
Familiarity with the City of Philadelphia and/or the SEPARTF is preferred. 
Experience with the THIRA / SPR, Homeland Security Grant Program, RCPGP, or NSGP is preferred. 
Experience conducting risk assessments, Strength – Weakness – Opportunities – Threats (SWOT) analysis, or other similar efforts is preferred.  
Experience interpreting and executing federal and state guidance is preferred. 
Experience coordinating large groups in collaborative, long-term, and recurring efforts is preferred.  
An equivalent combination of education and experience in a related field will be considered with approval by MDO-OEM and the Office of Human Resources. 

Licenses, Registrations, and Certification 

Possession of a valid proper class motor vehicle operator’s license issued by the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania within six months of hire. 
Successful completion of FEMA Independent Study courses (IS 100.a, 200.a, 700.a, and 800.b) within first month of appointment. 
Candidate will have access to secure public safety information.  All selected applicants must undergo and successfully complete a background investigation as a condition of placement in this position. 
Ability to obtain a security clearance.

Other Requirements 

Work may entail nights, weekends, and holidays. 
OEM personnel are essential, and work during states of emergency or other city closures. 
OEM personnel are required to serve periodically in an on-call capacity which may require the following conditions of work: work outside of typical business hours or for extended periods of time; work during states of emergency; work in a field environment, in a 24/7 watch center, or during activations of Philadelphia’s Emergency Operations Center (EOC). Example on-call work environments include, but are not limited to, scenes with the following conditions: materials that are on fire; utilities that are compromised; compromised structures; scenes near hazardous materials storage that may be compromised; scenes in congregate living settings, or in or near crowds; scenes near downed vegetation or other debris; or scenes near flooding and water-damaged materials. All work is performed while donning a level of personal protective equipment that 1) is recommended by the incident safety officer and 2) for which OEM personnel have received training. Example on-call response tasks include, but are not limited to, the following: working at a computer or with a portable tablet; observing and documenting conditions remotely or in the field; staffing an incident command post; communicating with responders or survivors; operating vehicles up to your licensed class; staffing facilities for survivors; transporting materials; being near a site where a serious injury or loss of life has occurred; sitting, standing, walking, climbing, crawling, or lifting or carrying materials. 
During times of disaster, work assignments, schedules, and reporting structures may be altered to meet the incident objectives. 
Full-time residency within the City of Philadelphia geographic boundaries required within six months of hire.  There are no exceptions to this policy. 
Ability to physically perform the duties during and outside of normal business hours while in or outdoors. 

Additional Information

TO APPLY:
Interested candidates must submit a cover letter, resume, writing sample, and references.

Salary Range: $85,000 - $94,500

Discover the Perks of Being a City of Philadelphia Employee:

Transportation: City employees get unlimited FREE public transportation all year long through SEPTA’s Key Advantage program. Employees can ride on SEPTA buses, subways, trolleys, and regional rail for their daily commute and more.
Parental Benefits: The City offers its employees 8 weeks of paid parental leave.

Unlock Tuition Discounts and Scholarships - The City of Philadelphia has forged partnerships with over a dozen esteemed colleges and universities in the area, ensuring that our employees have access to a wide range of tuition discounts and scholarships. Experience savings of 10% to 40% on your educational expenses, extending not only to City employees but in some cases, spouse and dependents too!

Join the City of Philadelphia team today and seize these incredible benefits designed to enhance your financial well-being and personal growth!

This position is ideal for project leaders who have successfully managed complex equipment manufacturing, delivery, installation, systems integration, infrastructure, construction, industrial automation, transportation, security technology, or defense projects in highly regulated environments.

Primary Responsibilities

Lead execution of complex Ports & Borders equipment delivery projects from contract award through customer acceptance and operational handoff. May also support Program Managers in execution of elements of their programs.
Serve as the primary customer interface and trusted advisor throughout the project lifecycle.
Own project cost, schedule, technical performance, risk management, and overall customer satisfaction.
Develop and maintain strong relationships with customers, suppliers, partners, and internal stakeholders.
Create and manage integrated project plans that align Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Installation, Quality, Finance, and Service activities.
Partner closely with Manufacturing and Production teams to ensure equipment is built, tested, and delivered according to project schedules and customer commitments.

Lead cross-functional teams in executing contractual obligations and achieving project milestones.

Manage project budgets, forecasts, profitability, and financial performance while maintaining ownership of project P&L.
Identify, assess, and mitigate project risks while driving timely resolution of issues impacting delivery.
Support business development activities, proposal efforts, contract negotiations, and growth opportunities with existing and prospective customers.
Develop executive-level project status reports and present performance updates to customers and senior leadership.
Monitor project readiness and proactively adjust plans to maintain schedule, cost, and quality objectives.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance delivery performance, customer satisfaction, operational efficiency, and project execution.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, integrity, and execution excellence.
Ensure compliance with contractual, regulatory, quality, and safety requirements.
Lead project execution through final customer acceptance and payment milestones.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's of Science degree in Engineering (Electrical, Mechanical, Industrial, Civil Engineering), Construction Management, Business Administration, Operations Management, Supply Chain, Project Management, or a related field.
Equivalent experience may be considered in lieu of a degree, including significant experience leading complex projects, construction projects, infrastructure deployments, capital equipment delivery, or technical operations.
10+ years of experience leading complex , projects, product delivery initiatives, construction projects, infrastructure deployments, or large-scale customer implementations.
Demonstrated success managing cross-functional teams within manufacturing, engineering, technology, construction, infrastructure, industrial, defense, transportation, security technology, or systems integration environments.
Experience managing customer-facing projects involving multiple stakeholders, competing priorities, and significant operational complexity.
Strong understanding of project financial management, forecasting, budgeting, profitability, earned value principles, and business performance metrics.
Experience coordinating manufacturing, supply chain, logistics, construction, installation, commissioning, and customer acceptance activities.
Strong negotiation, communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.
Proven ability to influence and lead within a matrixed organization without direct authority.
Experience working in regulated industries or environments with strict compliance requirements.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and modern project management tools.
Understanding of manufacturing operations, MRP/ERP systems, and configuration management principles.
Ability to travel up to 25% domestically and internationally.
Ability to obtain required customer and site access credentials, including U.S. Public Trust eligibility and customer security vetting requirements.
Work Location: This position requires on-site work at one of our designated locations: Vista, CA, or the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's of Science or Master's degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Engineering, Business, or a related discipline.
PMP (Project Management Professional), CCM (Certified Construction Manager), or equivalent project/program management certification.
Experience delivering Ports & Borders inspection systems, cargo inspection equipment, vehicle screening systems, X-ray imaging systems, radiation detection equipment, industrial automation systems, or other complex capital equipment.
Experience supporting U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Department of Homeland Security (DHS), international customs agencies, border security organizations, or similar government customers.
Experience leading infrastructure, transportation, port, border crossing, airport, or government-funded projects.
Knowledge of installation, commissioning, service, warranty, and lifecycle support operations.
Experience obtaining permits, licenses, certifications, and customer approvals required for complex equipment deployments.
Experience supporting proposal development, contract execution, and business growth initiatives.
Experience leading international projects and working within highly matrixed organizations.

Description

Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Tarrant County is seeking a motivated, experienced, and results-driven Program Manager (PM)
to provide leadership and oversight for our school-based program sites.

The Program Manager plays a vital role in ensuring high-quality programming, developing strong teams, and creating positive experiences for the youth and families we serve. This position provides strategic direction, operational support, and ongoing coaching to Site Coordinators and their teams while ensuring programs meet organizational goals, performance standards, and expectations.

The ideal candidate is a strong leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment, builds positive relationships, takes initiative, and is passionate about youth development. This individual will oversee multiple program sites, collaborate with school administrators and community partners, monitor program performance, and drive continuous improvement.

Position Details

Job Type:
Full Time - Hours vary based on program and operational needs.

The position requires coverage and availability during the following program hours:

Morning Shift: 6:30 AM – 8:00 AM

Afternoon Shift: 2:00 PM – 6:30 PM

Additional Hours: Additional daytime hours as needed for site visits, staff meetings, administrative responsibilities, training, and program oversight.

Flexibility is essential to meet the needs of assigned school-based program locations.

General Duties

Provide leadership and oversight for assigned program sites, ensuring alignment with organizational goals, policies, and strategic initiatives.
Guide Site Coordinators in developing, implementing, and monitoring site-specific operational plans and performance goals.
Establish and monitor program timelines, calendars, schedules, staffing plans, training activities, and deliverables.
Oversee daily program operations to ensure consistent implementation of programming, organizational standards, and best practices.
Monitor program performance, identify areas for improvement, and implement strategies to strengthen service delivery.
Communicate organizational updates, program expectations, marketing initiatives, and budget performance to Site Coordinators.
Ensure program activities align with the organization's mission, vision, and core values.

Staff Management

Supervise, coach, and support Site Coordinators and other assigned direct reports in achieving individual and organizational performance goals.
Ensure appropriate staffing levels across assigned sites and collaborate with leadership to address staffing needs.
Conduct annual and mid-year performance evaluations and establish development goals for direct reports.
Provide ongoing coaching, feedback, mentorship, and professional development opportunities.
Promote a culture of accountability, teamwork, recognition, and continuous improvement.
Empower site leadership to take ownership of daily operations, make informed decisions, and resolve challenges effectively.
Support recruitment, onboarding, orientation, and training of new employees, including shadowing and role-specific development.
Address performance concerns and provide appropriate guidance, corrective feedback, and follow-up.

Program Development

Monitor program quality, implementation, and compliance through regular site visits, observations, assessments, and evaluations.
Partner with the senior leadership to review program data, develop site report cards, and establish area-wide improvement plans.
Use observation results, participant feedback, surveys, and performance metrics to identify trends and opportunities for improvement.
Collaborate with the BGCGTC coaching team to provide technical assistance, coaching, and resources that enhance program quality and service delivery.
Monitor participant enrollment, attendance, engagement, and retention while identifying strategies to support recruitment and participation goals.
Coordinate the distribution of marketing and recruitment materials to support program awareness and enrollment.
Collect and review lesson plans, activity logs, and other program documentation to ensure consistent implementation and accountability.
Ensure program activities reflect the organization's mission and deliver meaningful outcomes for youth and families.

Administrative Compliance

Develop, monitor, and maintain site budgets in collaboration with organizational leadership.
Monitor expenditures, staffing costs, and program resources to ensure responsible financial management.
Review budget performance and communicate financial updates and recommendations to Site Coordinators.
Oversee the preparation and submission of required reports, documentation, and program performance data.
Ensure accurate and timely completion of administrative responsibilities, including Paylocity reporting and required documentation.
Create and manage site requisitions for new positions and collaborate with the Vice President of School Sites to maintain accurate staffing trackers.
Maintain accurate records related to enrollment, attendance, staffing, program activities, and operational performance.
Ensure all required organizational, contractual, and regulatory documentation is completed and maintained.
Monitor compliance with agency policies, procedures, minimum program standards, and applicable governing requirements.
Accountable for utilizing all BGCGTC communication tools regularly and effectively

Leadership

Self-Awareness: Ability to fully understand the impact emotions have on performance, assessment of strengths and weaknesses, relationships, and others. Demonstrates self-confidence, initiative, motivation, optimism and flexibility.
Self-Management: Ability to manage behaviors, thoughts, and emotions in a conscious and productive way. Models the ability to implement self-control in assessing frustrations and failures and models resilience and courage. Understands personal responsibility in different aspects of life and work, and what is needed to fulfill that responsibility.
Social Awareness: Ability to understand and learn about the diverse perspective of others. Includes listening, honoring others views, assessing impact of words, and the desire to serve others in effort to meet their needs appropriately and professionally.
Relationship Skills: Ability to build relationships which model caring, concern and healthy conflict. Demonstrates positive methods of collaboration and conflict resolution. Ability to positively lead and inspire others and integrate such models personally. Demonstrates ability to support positive work culture, which encourages results from others.
Responsible Decision Making: Ability to make constructive choices about personal behavior and social interactions based on ethical standards, safety concerns, and social norms; the realistic evaluation of consequences of various actions; and a consideration of the well-being of oneself and others

Facility & Safety

Accountable for adherence to all organizational health and safety policies and implementation of all safety practices and procedures at assigned work location(s)
Take all necessary and reasonable precautions to protect members, staff, equipment, materials, and facilities. Abide by facility maintenance protocols and procedures to ensure compliance
Accountable for reporting incidents and completing documentation within the required timeline
Maintain discipline, de-escalate conflict between members and/or others

Relationships

Be a positive role model
Maintain emotional control and make good decisions under pressure
Represent the Boys & Girls Club in a positive manner

Attendance

Regular attendance is required; arrive on time; punctuality is required

Nonessential Duties

Complete all other duties as assigned

Education and Work Experience Requirements:

Bachelor's degree in education, recreation, child development or related field preferred.
A minimum of 3 years of prior experience managing small to medium teams, as well as multi-site teams in a results-driven environment
Experience managing and leading people and learning the strengths and weaknesses of a team to put people in a position to succeed.
Experience in fiscal/budget management, data reporting, and management information systems.

Strong communication, public relations and interpersonal skills.
Strong organizational skills, including ability to plan for, implement, track, and evaluate programs and staff participation in those programs
Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, with all levels of internal and external stakeholders

Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.

At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth. We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.

We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan, which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.

Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride.

Departmental Overview

UC Berkeley is the flagship campus of the University of California, internationally renowned for intellectual endeavors, particularly in life sciences and engineering. To equip UC Berkeley with one of the finest global centers of innovation and entrepreneurship, the Bakar Bio Labs, Berkeley (BBLB) has been created as the flagship innovation center bringing together scholars, entrepreneurs, recent alumni, and industry – working at the interface of the life sciences and engineering – to translate their academic innovation out into the world as startups and as leaders. The mission of this unit is three-pronged: 1) Create essential & high visibility capabilities: rare, sought-after tough tech labs to attract industry and start-up innovators; 2) Chart a path for sustainable innovation for this generation and those to come: Establish a revenue-generating incubator that harnesses campus proximity and vibrant programs for students and researchers; and 3) Bolster our community and link to the greater world: Galvanize UC Berkeley's spokes of innovation and entrepreneurship, while providing a portal through which innovators from across UC, the State of California, and around the globe will join us.

Position Summary

The Business Operations Manager oversees and coordinates a full range of administrative operations for the Bakar Bio Labs, Berkeley, the incubator operating within the Bakar Labs overall ecosystem. The position is responsible for ensuring seamless day-to-day operations of the incubator. The responsibilities are significantly complex involving budgetary and financial management, real estate management, and professional communication with incubator staff and tenant companies.

Reporting to the Managing Director of Operations and Finance, the Business Operations Manager uses advanced administrative concepts and mature judgement to resolve complex issues and general administration management at a high level for Bakar Bio Labs, Berkeley. The incumbent develops, maintains, and modifies processes and procedures that sustain efficient operations. They regularly work on highly complex issues where analysis of situations or data requires an in-depth evaluation of variable factors and exercises judgment in selecting methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria for obtaining results. Poor decisions or failure to achieve goals may adversely affect the overall performance of the program.

The Business Operations Manager will supervise professional staff. Additionally, they lead and/or support activities related to purchasing, budget and resource management, communications, and facilities, and serve as the liaison for partners on purchasing, and reimbursements. The role includes responsibility for making office space assignments, oversight of tenant leases, and providing excellent support to existing and potential tenants.

Application Review Date

The First Review Date for this job is December 2, 2026. For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.

Responsibilities

Tenant Onboarding, Support, And Termination - 40%

In coordination with the incubator management team, make tenant space assignment recommendations and execute tenant lease/termination/amendments.
Maintain tenant leasing data including required insurance, lease end dates, and space assignments.
Manage cardkey assignments according to incubator staff and tenant staff changes.
Track tenant space assignments, the use of in-house premium services and adjustments.
Create and send invoices for monthly lease costs and monthly user services costs to appropriate tenant contact.
Ensure accuracy on invoiced amounts and follow up to ensure payment is timely and deposited into the correct Campus accounts.
Monitor all income from tenant leases, tenant premium services, and industry partnership revenue.
Recognize and take action to rectify irregularities.
Suggest concrete steps to enhance overall revenue.
At the direction of the Managing Director, perform and/or oversee special projects or assignments that are sensitive or complex in nature.
Manage all tenant and team interactions with a high degree of professionalism and a customer-service-oriented attitude.
Ensure tasks are completed in a timely manner.

Daily Office Operations And Facilities Management - 30%

Manage incubator-specific software (e.g., non-campus software like Airtable, Freshdesk, Skedda, Quickbooks, etc.)
Assist in technical troubleshooting on facility repairs/maintenance questions; project manage the resolution of facilities issues in a timely manner. The business operations manager will gain a high degree of familiarity with the facility to help make informed operational decisions.
Coordinate work with business operations managers at two (2) other incubators, across four (4) total facilities, across two (2) UC campuses. Identify potential efficiencies and provide recommendations to standardize policies, streamline cross-campus operations, and leverage shared operational resources.

Supervision of Direct Reports - 20%

Supervise a small group of professional staff in the areas of financial analysis, facilities, front desk and data support.
Provide operational guidance to team members as needed.
Lead administrative team to ensure all day-to-day issues are resolved in a timely manner.
Delegate tasks to team members, track progress, and ensure deadlines are met.
Coach employees as needed.
Handle escalations to the human resources team.

High Level Budgeting, Planning, And Cashflow Recording - 10%

Provide analysis for highly complex budgetary funding, capital, and operating projects, with multiple funding sources.
Assist the Managing Director with budget creation and reporting on key performance indicators. Represent the department on business affairs to the campus community.
Manage budget and forecast for the enterprise.
Report significant variances that impact operations.
Leverage existing purchasing and accounting campus resources to create processes which accurately and efficiently track all income and expenses for the incubator.

Required Qualifications

Advanced knowledge of a variety of administrative operational activities such as event planning, facilities management, risk management planning, tenant/vendor management, accounting and payroll, and contracts regulations and guidelines.
Advanced interpersonal skills including verbal and written communication, active listening, critical thinking, persuasiveness, advising and counseling skills.
Ability to use discretion and maintain confidentiality.
Advanced skills in short- and long-term strategic planning, analysis, problem-solving and customer service.
Advanced knowledge of financial analysis and reporting techniques, and / or human resources policies and procedures for staff and academic employees.

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced knowledge of and/or ability to learn University rules and regulations, processes, protocols and procedures for budget, accounting and fund management, and / or personnel management.
Advanced knowledge of and/or ability to learn common University-specific computer application programs.

Education / Training

Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training. (Required)

Salary & Benefits

For information on the comprehensive benefits package offered by the University, please visit the University of California's Compensation & Benefits website.

Under California law, the University of California, Berkeley is required to provide a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role and should not offer a salary outside of the range posted in this job announcement. This range takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions, including but not limited to experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, analysis of internal equity, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be offered a salary at or near the top of the range for a position. Salary offers are determined based on final candidate qualifications and experience.

The budgeted annual salary range that the University reasonably expects to pay for this position is $120,000.00 - $170,000.00.

This is an exempt, monthly-paid position.
This is a full-time (40 hours/week) Career position eligible for UC benefits.

How To Apply

To apply, please submit your resume and cover letter.

Other Information

This position is eligible for up to 1 day/week remote work within the United States. Exact arrangements are determined in partnership with your supervisor to meet role responsibilities and department needs and are subject to change.
This is not a visa opportunity. This position does not include sponsorship of a new consular H-1B visa petition that would require payment of the $100,000 supplemental fee.
Travel requirement (5%) - Conference attendance as needed.

Conviction History Background

This is a designated position requiring fingerprinting and a background check due to the nature of the job responsibilities. Berkeley does hire people with conviction histories and reviews information received in the context of the job responsibilities. The University reserves the right to make employment contingent upon successful completion of the background check.

Mandated Reporter

This position has been identified as a Mandated Reporter required to report the observed or suspected abuse or neglect of children, dependent adults, or elders to designated law enforcement or social service agencies. We reserve the right to make employment contingent upon completion of signed statements acknowledging the responsibilities of a Mandated Reporter.

Misconduct

jobs.title: Corporate Security Manager
jobs.description:
About The Company

Se para você a tecnologia existe para melhorar o caminho da vida, para o nosso time também: Seu Caminho, Nossa Jornada.

Acreditamos na tecnologia que conecta gente boa no que faz e que vive a diversidade para criar e compartilhar até os caminhos que a gente (ainda!) nem sabe quais são. Trabalhamos para gerar valor não só para os nossos usuários, mas, sobretudo, para as comunidades que servimos e toda a sociedade, tornando a vida das pessoas melhor com serviços que facilitem seu dia a dia - seja com serviços de mobilidade e entrega (99) ou pagamentos digitais (99Pay).

Para facilitar a vida de milhões de pessoas todos os dias, desde 2018 fazemos parte da DiDi Global Inc., a maior plataforma de tecnologia e transporte por aplicativo do mundo. Somos pioneiros na criação de soluções inovadoras que começam no Brasil e que ganham escala para gerar impacto positivo em mais de 12 países em que a DiDi está presente. Essas inovações passam por sustentabilidade, segurança, inteligência artificial, mercado financeiro e um tanto mais.

Seja para construir projetos do zero ou aprimorar nossas soluções, gostamos de desafios que nos fazem sentir frio na barriga, e é por isso que trabalhamos num ritmo acelerado, com respeito, colaboração e bom humor. Nessa jornada, também nos fortalecemos nas diferentes vivências e opiniões para crescermos juntos, errar rápido, aprender e ajustar o caminho para criar soluções que tragam ainda melhores resultados.

About The Team/role

Como Gerente de Segurança Corporativa, o(a) profissional será responsável por liderar a estratégia e as operações de segurança da 99/DiDi no Brasil, assegurando a proteção integral de pessoas, instalações, ativos corporativos e a continuidade dos negócios por meio de uma abordagem orientada por dados e excelência operacional.

Integrando a estrutura global de Segurança Corporativa da 99/DiDi, a posição liderará as operações de segurança no país e o DiDi Intelligence and Security Operations Center (DiSOC), coordenará a resposta a crises e incidentes críticos e atuará como parceiro estratégico das lideranças locais e globais. Também será responsável pela articulação com áreas parceiras, como EHS e Facilities, para fortalecer a gestão integrada de riscos, a proteção dos ambientes corporativos e a continuidade das operações.

In this role, you'll be...

Liderar a equipe de Corporate Security no Brasil, fornecendo tanto direcionamento estratégico quanto orientação prática aos membros do time para lidar eficazmente com questões relacionadas à segurança.
Gerenciar as operações diárias do Security Operations Center da DiDi (DiSOC) no Brasil.
Acompanhar KPIs, métricas e acordos de nível de serviço (SLAs) de segurança para mensurar a eficácia dos programas e impulsionar a melhoria contínua.
Gerenciar orçamentos de segurança, quadro de funcionários e projetos estratégicos, garantindo a entrega no prazo e dentro do orçamento, otimizando recursos por meio de tomada de decisão orientada por dados.
Executar avaliações de risco e coordenar operações de segurança para eventos corporativos, visitas executivas e inaugurações de novas instalações, atuando em parceria com EHS para garantir conformidade regulatória.
Responder a emergências e eventos críticos de segurança conforme necessário.
Desenvolver e apresentar comunicações, relatórios e briefings claros para nível executivo, traduzindo dados de segurança em percepções e direcionamentos estratégicos de negócios.

We're eager to be in touch because you have...

Ensino superior completo em Administração, Direito, Gestão de Segurança, Relações Internacionais, Engenharia ou áreas correlatas.
Vivência sênior/consolidada em Segurança Corporativa (Corporate Security), incluindo experiência comprovada em liderança e desenvolvimento de equipes.
Experiência prática na gestão ou coordenação de Centros de Operações de Segurança (SOC) e resposta a incidentes críticos/emergências.
Vivência na condução de análises de risco patrimonial/pessoal, proteção executiva e segurança em grandes eventos e instalações prediais.
Habilidade para gerenciar orçamentos (Capex/Opex), contratação/gestão de fornecedores e controle de métricas/KPIs operacionais.
Inglês avançado ou fluente para comunicação diária com lideranças e equipes globais (relatórios, reuniões e alinhamentos corporativos).
Flexibilidade para atuar em eventuais chamados e respostas a emergências fora do horário comercial.

You'll love working at DiDi because...

We create user value

We strive to always create valuable experiences for our users in everything we do. Our focus is to always innovate new experiences that are safe, pleasant and efficient.

We are data-driven

We are strong believers in making informed decisions, that’s why we are data-driven. We can better navigate the business landscape strategically by analyzing valuable metrics.

Win-win Collaboration

Success is a team sport. When we work to help our partners and colleagues win, we win, too. While keeping everyone's best interest at heart, we communicate with candor and execute with excellence in all we do.

We believe in integrity

Integrity is at the very core of our business. We are people who always want to do the right thing. Our intentions are sincere, we speak our minds and listen to each other.

Growth

We always strive to do better. That means venturing beyond our comfort zones, learning from our mistakes, and helping each other grow.

Diversity and Inclusion

Diversity is one of our biggest strengths. Our differences are what make us distinct. We respect each other and believe in equal opportunities for all.

Diversity & Inclusion

Diversity is not a vision of the future or something we wish to have one day, it is a non-negotiable value of who we are.

We practice inclusion, plurality, and respect. And we count on the governance of the Diversity Committee, which works together with HR, leadership and identity groups - 99Adapta, 99Afro, 99Cores, 99Mulheres, and 99Mamães. This part of our journey has been written, there remains a long road before us.

We reinforce that this position is open to everyone, including pregnant people and people with disabilities (PwD).

At CGI, our Project Managers turn complex transformation into measurable outcomes. You’ll have the ownership to shape delivery, apply creative thinking to solve challenges and help introduce safe, production-ready change in a highly regulated setting. Working alongside CGI and client experts, you’ll combine robust governance with Agile techniques where appropriate, supported by CGI’s proven methods, global delivery capability and deep sector expertise. This is an opportunity to influence critical transformation, strengthen client outcomes and grow your career within a collaborative community that supports you to succeed.

CGI was recognised in the Sunday Times Best Places to Work List 2025 and has been named a UK ‘Best Employer’ by the Financial Times. We offer a competitive salary, excellent pension, private healthcare, plus a share scheme (3.5% + 3.5% matching) which makes you a CGI Partner not just an employee. We are committed to inclusivity, building a genuinely diverse community of tech talent and inspiring everyone to pursue careers in our sector, including our Armed Forces, and are proud to hold a Gold Award in recognition of our support of the Armed Forces Corporate Covenant. Join us and you’ll be part of an open, friendly community of experts. We’ll train and support you in taking your career wherever you want it to go.

This is a hybrid role is based in Aberdeen and requires regular on-site presence, typically three days per week, enabling close collaboration with CGI and client teams.

Candidate Profile

In this role, you will take ownership of planning and delivering complex IT integration and transformation projects, providing the structure, governance and momentum needed to achieve successful outcomes. Working within client PMO and stage-gate processes, you will coordinate cross-functional teams spanning ERP, Operations/HSE, infrastructure and Digital & Analytics while maintaining clear oversight of scope, budgets, risks and dependencies.

You will build trusted relationships across business and IT teams, creating an environment where ideas can be explored, challenges resolved and informed decisions made. Supported by CGI’s collaborative community and established delivery methods, you will coordinate multiple suppliers and help ensure changes to production and HSE-critical systems are introduced safely and successfully.

Plan & Govern: Own project plans, budgets, RAID controls, reporting and governance across multiple workstreams.
Lead & Coordinate: Bring together cross-functional teams, establishing clear scope, dependencies, responsibilities and hand-offs.
Manage Risk & Vendors: Proactively address risks, issues and dependencies while coordinating CGI, client and third-party suppliers.
Engage & Influence: Build strong relationships with business and IT stakeholders, manage expectations and facilitate effective decision-making.
Deliver Change Safely: Lead cutover, go-live and hypercare planning, ensuring robust runbooks and effective transition into BAU.
Improve & Innovate: Apply proven CGI methods, metrics and lessons learned while identifying creative opportunities to improve delivery effectiveness.

Required Qualifications To Be Successful In This Role

You will bring substantial experience managing medium-to-large IT projects, ideally involving integration, migration or transformation within energy, utilities or another complex environment. You will be confident combining structured governance with strong commercial, stakeholder and delivery management, while working collaboratively across technical teams and multiple suppliers.

Essential certification: PRINCE2 Practitioner or PMP.
Project experience: Experience in IT project delivery, including large-scale integration, migration or transformation.
Governance: Strong experience of project governance, stage-gate delivery, RAID management and project reporting.
Commercial management: Proven capability in budget control, financial tracking and third-party/vendor management.
Stakeholder leadership: Strong ability to engage and influence senior business and IT stakeholders in complex environments.
Multi-vendor delivery: Proven experience coordinating multiple technical teams, suppliers and delivery dependencies.
Sector knowledge: Oil & Gas or wider energy-sector experience is preferred.
Functional knowledge: Relevant experience aligned to the project area, such as SAP/ERP project management or infrastructure/IM delivery.
Additional qualifications: ITIL Foundation and Agile/Scrum certification are desirable.

jobs.title: Business Process Engineer and Project Manager
jobs.description:
About us

110 Analytics builds the data platforms, operational systems and AI that organisations run on. With our platform engineering team we take a client from a first conversation to a live system, fast, across many industries.

The role

You make our clients' work run better, and you get it delivered. Half process engineer, half project manager.

You map how an organisation really works today, find where time, money and information leak, and design how it should run: the workflow, the rules, the hand-offs, the automation and the measures that prove it works. Then you run the project that puts it live: plan, people, scope, risks and dates, until the client uses it every day.

What you own

Process discovery: workshops and shadowing with the people who do the work, until you can draw their process better than they can
Process design: as-is and to-be maps in BPMN or similar, with the rules, roles, exceptions, service levels and KPIs written down
Automation: deciding what the system does, what people do and what AI does, then specifying the workflows, forms, approvals and integrations our engineers build or you configure yourself
The project plan: scope, milestones, sprints, dependencies and resourcing, kept current and honest
Delivery: stand-ups, client status meetings, risks, issues and change requests, with scope and dates protected
Go-live: testing, training, cut-over and the first weeks live, then proving the new process beats the old one
Several projects in flight at once, each with a clear plan

Who you are

Three to seven years in process improvement, process engineering, business analysis or project management, on real client or operations projects
You have taken at least one process change from the first map to go-live and can show the before and after
Fluent in process notation (BPMN, swimlanes, value stream maps) and at home in a project plan (Gantt, Kanban, sprints)
Comfortable with workflow, low-code, ERP or automation platforms. You do not need to code, but you understand data, integrations and APIs well enough to brief an engineer
Organised without being bureaucratic. Plans exist to get things live
Calm in front of senior clients, able to say no and keep them on side
Lean, Six Sigma, PMP, PRINCE2 or Agile certification is a plus, not a requirement
Fluent English. Maltese is a plus

How we work

Small team, real ownership, no politics. Many industries, so no two projects are the same. AI-first: you will use AI every day for discovery notes, process drafts, plans and status reports, and we show you how in week one.

You get direction. The plan is yours.

Pay

Base salary EUR 40,000 to 55,000 a year, depending on experience.

How to apply

Apply with Easy Apply. If you add a note, tell us in three lines about one process you changed: how it ran before, what you did, and how it ran after.

The process: a short call, then one live working session where we play a client with a messy process and you map it and plan the fix. Nothing to prepare. It moves fast, and you hear from a person either way.

Primary Purpose

The Special Activities and Intelligence (SAI) team in CNA’s Operational Warfighting division is seeking an applied scientist with a background in cognitive or behavioral science, neuroscience, or psychology.
Experience, background, or interest in human decision making, cognitive load, interaction effects with artificial intelligence, and/or human decision aids and tools is a plus.

Applicants should possess or be nearing completion of a PhD in cognitive neuroscience, psychology, or related field and have an interest in applied, operations or policy-oriented research and the ability to write, speak, and present to both technical and non-technical audiences in a clear and concise format. Applicants should also have:

Strong analytic curiosity and creativity;
The ability to operate both independently and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary environment;
Strong critical thinking skills;
Knowledge of relevant research techniques and recent advancements;
Strong planning and organizational skills;
Excellent interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills; and
The ability to interact positively and somewhat independently with clients.

Strong consideration will be given to applicants with experience with quantitative methodologies, stochastic modeling and simulation, and/or statistics.

As part of the Department of Navy’s Federally Funded Research and Development Center (FFRDC), CNA’s Operational Warfighting Division provides analysis that helps naval warfighters organize, plan, train, and execute their missions. The Special Activities and Intelligence program conducts operational assessments of how warfighters can synchronize maneuver and non-kinetic effects, integrate operational teams across domains and echelons, and optimize the extraction of operational value from information and intelligence feeds to provide decision advantage.

As a Research Analyst
, you will provide analysis to help develop and evaluate how commanders see, understand, and decide at the operational level of war; identify cross-domain advantages or dependencies; and craft policies, concepts, and requirements for synchronized effects. Major research areas include the application, integration, and assessment of artificial intelligence, autonomy, and multi-INT sensor fusion for command and control, integrated fires, data governance and interoperability, and special operations.

Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst

The Opportunity:

As a cyber threat intel analyst, you know the key to detecting and deterring malicious activity is quality risk-based intel that maps to a tactical behavior. At Booz Allen, you can apply your skills and experience to help investigate the most pressing cyber threats impacting financial services. This is your chance to take on the adversary’s perspective, identify their motivations, and recommend ways to harden systems, reduce their attack surface, and thwart malicious actors.

As a Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst on our team, you’ll be trusted to collect, document, assess, and analyze raw cyber threat information using tools and technologies such as MITRE Attack Framework to enrich intelligence. You’ll help conduct strategic assessments on systems and networks and provide tactical analyses and influential recommendations for network operation. You’ll be the key to discovering and correlating timely threat intel and deciphering what represents a real risk, and you’ll play an active role in incident analysis and producing intelligence products to inform cyber operators.

Cyber threats are evolving. Booz Allen is committed to creating an environment where you not only keep pace with the industry but propel it forward. With access to academic programs, certifications, and opportunities to use expert tradecraft, we’ll continuously invest in you so you can create the career you want as you grow.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

You Have: 

2+ years of experience in cyber threat intelligence, intelligence analysis, or data science and analysis
Experience collaborating with multiple internal and external stakeholders to gather data and intelligence, analyze, vet, and enrich intelligence, create joint reports, and share with stakeholders
Experience writing succinct briefings, presentations, and reports to convey analysis, threat trends, threat actor profiles, indicator bulletins, vulnerability details, and defensive strategies
Knowledge of cyber threats, open-source research, and nation state actors
Ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust or Suitability/Fitness determination based on client requirements
Bachelor's degree

Nice If You Have: 

Experience with Threat Intel Platforms (TIP) such as OpenCTI or other threat data repositories
Experience working in a fast-paced, cyber threat or analysis center, promptly responding to critical mission needs
Knowledge of threat intelligence research and data enrichment, including performing WhoIs or DNS lookups and querying existing threat repositories and new sources for additional data correlation
Knowledge of current and emerging cyber adversaries and their TTPs
Knowledge of threat modeling and adversary tactics and techniques frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK matrices, Cyber Kill Chain, STRIDE, or PASTA
Ability to adopt adversary perspective analyzing targeted cyberspace to predict adversary courses of action in support of tactical to operational planning efforts
GCTI, GSEC, SEC+, or CEH Certification

Vetting:

Full-time and part-time employees working at least 20 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in Booz Allen’s benefit programs. Individuals that do not meet the threshold are only eligible for select offerings, not inclusive of health benefits. We encourage you to learn more about our total benefits by visiting the Resource page on our Careers site and reviewing Our Employee Benefits page.
