Description

Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Tarrant County is seeking a motivated, experienced, and results-driven Program Manager (PM)
to provide leadership and oversight for our school-based program sites.

The Program Manager plays a vital role in ensuring high-quality programming, developing strong teams, and creating positive experiences for the youth and families we serve. This position provides strategic direction, operational support, and ongoing coaching to Site Coordinators and their teams while ensuring programs meet organizational goals, performance standards, and expectations.

The ideal candidate is a strong leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment, builds positive relationships, takes initiative, and is passionate about youth development. This individual will oversee multiple program sites, collaborate with school administrators and community partners, monitor program performance, and drive continuous improvement.

Position Details

Job Type:
Full Time - Hours vary based on program and operational needs.

The position requires coverage and availability during the following program hours:

Morning Shift: 6:30 AM – 8:00 AM

Afternoon Shift: 2:00 PM – 6:30 PM

Additional Hours: Additional daytime hours as needed for site visits, staff meetings, administrative responsibilities, training, and program oversight.

Flexibility is essential to meet the needs of assigned school-based program locations.

General Duties

Provide leadership and oversight for assigned program sites, ensuring alignment with organizational goals, policies, and strategic initiatives.
Guide Site Coordinators in developing, implementing, and monitoring site-specific operational plans and performance goals.
Establish and monitor program timelines, calendars, schedules, staffing plans, training activities, and deliverables.
Oversee daily program operations to ensure consistent implementation of programming, organizational standards, and best practices.
Monitor program performance, identify areas for improvement, and implement strategies to strengthen service delivery.
Communicate organizational updates, program expectations, marketing initiatives, and budget performance to Site Coordinators.
Ensure program activities align with the organization's mission, vision, and core values.

Staff Management

Supervise, coach, and support Site Coordinators and other assigned direct reports in achieving individual and organizational performance goals.
Ensure appropriate staffing levels across assigned sites and collaborate with leadership to address staffing needs.
Conduct annual and mid-year performance evaluations and establish development goals for direct reports.
Provide ongoing coaching, feedback, mentorship, and professional development opportunities.
Promote a culture of accountability, teamwork, recognition, and continuous improvement.
Empower site leadership to take ownership of daily operations, make informed decisions, and resolve challenges effectively.
Support recruitment, onboarding, orientation, and training of new employees, including shadowing and role-specific development.
Address performance concerns and provide appropriate guidance, corrective feedback, and follow-up.

Program Development

Monitor program quality, implementation, and compliance through regular site visits, observations, assessments, and evaluations.
Partner with the senior leadership to review program data, develop site report cards, and establish area-wide improvement plans.
Use observation results, participant feedback, surveys, and performance metrics to identify trends and opportunities for improvement.
Collaborate with the BGCGTC coaching team to provide technical assistance, coaching, and resources that enhance program quality and service delivery.
Monitor participant enrollment, attendance, engagement, and retention while identifying strategies to support recruitment and participation goals.
Coordinate the distribution of marketing and recruitment materials to support program awareness and enrollment.
Collect and review lesson plans, activity logs, and other program documentation to ensure consistent implementation and accountability.
Ensure program activities reflect the organization's mission and deliver meaningful outcomes for youth and families.

Administrative Compliance

Develop, monitor, and maintain site budgets in collaboration with organizational leadership.
Monitor expenditures, staffing costs, and program resources to ensure responsible financial management.
Review budget performance and communicate financial updates and recommendations to Site Coordinators.
Oversee the preparation and submission of required reports, documentation, and program performance data.
Ensure accurate and timely completion of administrative responsibilities, including Paylocity reporting and required documentation.
Create and manage site requisitions for new positions and collaborate with the Vice President of School Sites to maintain accurate staffing trackers.
Maintain accurate records related to enrollment, attendance, staffing, program activities, and operational performance.
Ensure all required organizational, contractual, and regulatory documentation is completed and maintained.
Monitor compliance with agency policies, procedures, minimum program standards, and applicable governing requirements.
Accountable for utilizing all BGCGTC communication tools regularly and effectively

Leadership

Self-Awareness: Ability to fully understand the impact emotions have on performance, assessment of strengths and weaknesses, relationships, and others. Demonstrates self-confidence, initiative, motivation, optimism and flexibility.
Self-Management: Ability to manage behaviors, thoughts, and emotions in a conscious and productive way. Models the ability to implement self-control in assessing frustrations and failures and models resilience and courage. Understands personal responsibility in different aspects of life and work, and what is needed to fulfill that responsibility.
Social Awareness: Ability to understand and learn about the diverse perspective of others. Includes listening, honoring others views, assessing impact of words, and the desire to serve others in effort to meet their needs appropriately and professionally.
Relationship Skills: Ability to build relationships which model caring, concern and healthy conflict. Demonstrates positive methods of collaboration and conflict resolution. Ability to positively lead and inspire others and integrate such models personally. Demonstrates ability to support positive work culture, which encourages results from others.
Responsible Decision Making: Ability to make constructive choices about personal behavior and social interactions based on ethical standards, safety concerns, and social norms; the realistic evaluation of consequences of various actions; and a consideration of the well-being of oneself and others

Facility & Safety

Accountable for adherence to all organizational health and safety policies and implementation of all safety practices and procedures at assigned work location(s)
Take all necessary and reasonable precautions to protect members, staff, equipment, materials, and facilities. Abide by facility maintenance protocols and procedures to ensure compliance
Accountable for reporting incidents and completing documentation within the required timeline
Maintain discipline, de-escalate conflict between members and/or others

Relationships

Maintain emotional control and make good decisions under pressure
Represent the Boys & Girls Club in a positive manner

Attendance

Regular attendance is required; arrive on time; punctuality is required

Nonessential Duties

Complete all other duties as assigned

Requirements

Education and Work Experience Requirements:

Bachelor's degree in education, recreation, child development or related field preferred.
A minimum of 3 years of prior experience managing small to medium teams, as well as multi-site teams in a results-driven environment
Experience managing and leading people and learning the strengths and weaknesses of a team to put people in a position to succeed.
Experience in fiscal/budget management, data reporting, and management information systems.

Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, with all levels of internal and external stakeholders

new_jobs.description:
About Berkeley

At the University of California, Berkeley, we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.

At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth. We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.

We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan, which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.

Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride.

Departmental Overview

UC Berkeley is the flagship campus of the University of California, internationally renowned for intellectual endeavors, particularly in life sciences and engineering. To equip UC Berkeley with one of the finest global centers of innovation and entrepreneurship, the Bakar Bio Labs, Berkeley (BBLB) has been created as the flagship innovation center bringing together scholars, entrepreneurs, recent alumni, and industry – working at the interface of the life sciences and engineering – to translate their academic innovation out into the world as startups and as leaders. The mission of this unit is three-pronged: 1) Create essential & high visibility capabilities: rare, sought-after tough tech labs to attract industry and start-up innovators; 2) Chart a path for sustainable innovation for this generation and those to come: Establish a revenue-generating incubator that harnesses campus proximity and vibrant programs for students and researchers; and 3) Bolster our community and link to the greater world: Galvanize UC Berkeley's spokes of innovation and entrepreneurship, while providing a portal through which innovators from across UC, the State of California, and around the globe will join us.

Position Summary

The Business Operations Manager oversees and coordinates a full range of administrative operations for the Bakar Bio Labs, Berkeley, the incubator operating within the Bakar Labs overall ecosystem. The position is responsible for ensuring seamless day-to-day operations of the incubator. The responsibilities are significantly complex involving budgetary and financial management, real estate management, and professional communication with incubator staff and tenant companies.

Reporting to the Managing Director of Operations and Finance, the Business Operations Manager uses advanced administrative concepts and mature judgement to resolve complex issues and general administration management at a high level for Bakar Bio Labs, Berkeley. The incumbent develops, maintains, and modifies processes and procedures that sustain efficient operations. They regularly work on highly complex issues where analysis of situations or data requires an in-depth evaluation of variable factors and exercises judgment in selecting methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria for obtaining results. Poor decisions or failure to achieve goals may adversely affect the overall performance of the program.

The Business Operations Manager will supervise professional staff. Additionally, they lead and/or support activities related to purchasing, budget and resource management, communications, and facilities, and serve as the liaison for partners on purchasing, and reimbursements. The role includes responsibility for making office space assignments, oversight of tenant leases, and providing excellent support to existing and potential tenants.

Application Review Date

The First Review Date for this job is December 2, 2026. For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.

Responsibilities

Tenant Onboarding, Support, And Termination - 40%

In coordination with the incubator management team, make tenant space assignment recommendations and execute tenant lease/termination/amendments.
Maintain tenant leasing data including required insurance, lease end dates, and space assignments.
Manage cardkey assignments according to incubator staff and tenant staff changes.
Track tenant space assignments, the use of in-house premium services and adjustments.
Create and send invoices for monthly lease costs and monthly user services costs to appropriate tenant contact.
Ensure accuracy on invoiced amounts and follow up to ensure payment is timely and deposited into the correct Campus accounts.
Monitor all income from tenant leases, tenant premium services, and industry partnership revenue.
Recognize and take action to rectify irregularities.
Suggest concrete steps to enhance overall revenue.
At the direction of the Managing Director, perform and/or oversee special projects or assignments that are sensitive or complex in nature.
Manage all tenant and team interactions with a high degree of professionalism and a customer-service-oriented attitude.
Ensure tasks are completed in a timely manner.

Daily Office Operations And Facilities Management - 30%

Manage incubator-specific software (e.g., non-campus software like Airtable, Freshdesk, Skedda, Quickbooks, etc.)
Assist in technical troubleshooting on facility repairs/maintenance questions; project manage the resolution of facilities issues in a timely manner. The business operations manager will gain a high degree of familiarity with the facility to help make informed operational decisions.
Coordinate work with business operations managers at two (2) other incubators, across four (4) total facilities, across two (2) UC campuses. Identify potential efficiencies and provide recommendations to standardize policies, streamline cross-campus operations, and leverage shared operational resources.

Supervision of Direct Reports - 20%

Supervise a small group of professional staff in the areas of financial analysis, facilities, front desk and data support.
Provide operational guidance to team members as needed.
Lead administrative team to ensure all day-to-day issues are resolved in a timely manner.
Delegate tasks to team members, track progress, and ensure deadlines are met.
Coach employees as needed.
Handle escalations to the human resources team.

High Level Budgeting, Planning, And Cashflow Recording - 10%

Provide analysis for highly complex budgetary funding, capital, and operating projects, with multiple funding sources.
Assist the Managing Director with budget creation and reporting on key performance indicators. Represent the department on business affairs to the campus community.
Manage budget and forecast for the enterprise.
Report significant variances that impact operations.
Leverage existing purchasing and accounting campus resources to create processes which accurately and efficiently track all income and expenses for the incubator.

Required Qualifications

Advanced knowledge of a variety of administrative operational activities such as event planning, facilities management, risk management planning, tenant/vendor management, accounting and payroll, and contracts regulations and guidelines.
Advanced interpersonal skills including verbal and written communication, active listening, critical thinking, persuasiveness, advising and counseling skills.
Ability to use discretion and maintain confidentiality.
Advanced skills in short- and long-term strategic planning, analysis, problem-solving and customer service.
Advanced knowledge of financial analysis and reporting techniques, and / or human resources policies and procedures for staff and academic employees.

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced knowledge of and/or ability to learn University rules and regulations, processes, protocols and procedures for budget, accounting and fund management, and / or personnel management.
Advanced knowledge of and/or ability to learn common University-specific computer application programs.

Education / Training

Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training. (Required)

Salary & Benefits

For information on the comprehensive benefits package offered by the University, please visit the University of California's Compensation & Benefits website.

Under California law, the University of California, Berkeley is required to provide a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role and should not offer a salary outside of the range posted in this job announcement. This range takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions, including but not limited to experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, analysis of internal equity, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be offered a salary at or near the top of the range for a position. Salary offers are determined based on final candidate qualifications and experience.

The budgeted annual salary range that the University reasonably expects to pay for this position is $120,000.00 - $170,000.00.

This is an exempt, monthly-paid position.
This is a full-time (40 hours/week) Career position eligible for UC benefits.

How To Apply

To apply, please submit your resume and cover letter.

Other Information

This position is eligible for up to 1 day/week remote work within the United States. Exact arrangements are determined in partnership with your supervisor to meet role responsibilities and department needs and are subject to change.
This is not a visa opportunity. This position does not include sponsorship of a new consular H-1B visa petition that would require payment of the $100,000 supplemental fee.
Travel requirement (5%) - Conference attendance as needed.

Conviction History Background

This is a designated position requiring fingerprinting and a background check due to the nature of the job responsibilities. Berkeley does hire people with conviction histories and reviews information received in the context of the job responsibilities. The University reserves the right to make employment contingent upon successful completion of the background check.

Mandated Reporter

This position has been identified as a Mandated Reporter required to report the observed or suspected abuse or neglect of children, dependent adults, or elders to designated law enforcement or social service agencies. We reserve the right to make employment contingent upon completion of signed statements acknowledging the responsibilities of a Mandated Reporter.

About us

110 Analytics builds the data platforms, operational systems and AI that organisations run on. With our platform engineering team we take a client from a first conversation to a live system, fast, across many industries.

The role

You make our clients' work run better, and you get it delivered. Half process engineer, half project manager.

You map how an organisation really works today, find where time, money and information leak, and design how it should run: the workflow, the rules, the hand-offs, the automation and the measures that prove it works. Then you run the project that puts it live: plan, people, scope, risks and dates, until the client uses it every day.

What you own

Process discovery: workshops and shadowing with the people who do the work, until you can draw their process better than they can
Process design: as-is and to-be maps in BPMN or similar, with the rules, roles, exceptions, service levels and KPIs written down
Automation: deciding what the system does, what people do and what AI does, then specifying the workflows, forms, approvals and integrations our engineers build or you configure yourself
The project plan: scope, milestones, sprints, dependencies and resourcing, kept current and honest
Delivery: stand-ups, client status meetings, risks, issues and change requests, with scope and dates protected
Go-live: testing, training, cut-over and the first weeks live, then proving the new process beats the old one
Several projects in flight at once, each with a clear plan

Who you are

Three to seven years in process improvement, process engineering, business analysis or project management, on real client or operations projects
You have taken at least one process change from the first map to go-live and can show the before and after
Fluent in process notation (BPMN, swimlanes, value stream maps) and at home in a project plan (Gantt, Kanban, sprints)
Comfortable with workflow, low-code, ERP or automation platforms. You do not need to code, but you understand data, integrations and APIs well enough to brief an engineer
Organised without being bureaucratic. Plans exist to get things live
Calm in front of senior clients, able to say no and keep them on side
Lean, Six Sigma, PMP, PRINCE2 or Agile certification is a plus, not a requirement
Fluent English. Maltese is a plus

How we work

Small team, real ownership, no politics. Many industries, so no two projects are the same. AI-first: you will use AI every day for discovery notes, process drafts, plans and status reports, and we show you how in week one.

You get direction. The plan is yours.

Pay

Base salary EUR 40,000 to 55,000 a year, depending on experience.

How to apply

Apply with Easy Apply. If you add a note, tell us in three lines about one process you changed: how it ran before, what you did, and how it ran after.

The process: a short call, then one live working session where we play a client with a messy process and you map it and plan the fix. Nothing to prepare. It moves fast, and you hear from a person either way.

Primary Purpose

The Special Activities and Intelligence (SAI) team in CNA’s Operational Warfighting division is seeking an applied scientist with a background in cognitive or behavioral science, neuroscience, or psychology.
Experience, background, or interest in human decision making, cognitive load, interaction effects with artificial intelligence, and/or human decision aids and tools is a plus.

Applicants should possess or be nearing completion of a PhD in cognitive neuroscience, psychology, or related field and have an interest in applied, operations or policy-oriented research and the ability to write, speak, and present to both technical and non-technical audiences in a clear and concise format. Applicants should also have:

Strong analytic curiosity and creativity;
The ability to operate both independently and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary environment;
Strong critical thinking skills;
Knowledge of relevant research techniques and recent advancements;
Strong planning and organizational skills;
Excellent interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills; and
The ability to interact positively and somewhat independently with clients.

Strong consideration will be given to applicants with experience with quantitative methodologies, stochastic modeling and simulation, and/or statistics.

As part of the Department of Navy’s Federally Funded Research and Development Center (FFRDC), CNA’s Operational Warfighting Division provides analysis that helps naval warfighters organize, plan, train, and execute their missions. The Special Activities and Intelligence program conducts operational assessments of how warfighters can synchronize maneuver and non-kinetic effects, integrate operational teams across domains and echelons, and optimize the extraction of operational value from information and intelligence feeds to provide decision advantage.

As a Research Analyst
, you will provide analysis to help develop and evaluate how commanders see, understand, and decide at the operational level of war; identify cross-domain advantages or dependencies; and craft policies, concepts, and requirements for synchronized effects. Major research areas include the application, integration, and assessment of artificial intelligence, autonomy, and multi-INT sensor fusion for command and control, integrated fires, data governance and interoperability, and special operations.

CNA fosters an inclusive culture that values diverse backgrounds and perspectives. Our flexible and engaging work environment encourages iterative and creative collaboration at every stage of the problem solving process. Our employees are committed to helping clients develop effective solutions to better manage their programs through scientific, data-driven approaches. We are looking for creative and innovative individuals to help carry out our mission.

About The Role

We are looking for a Senior Security Operations Analyst to serve as our primary operational anchor for EMEA, bridging follow-the-sun operations across global time zones (APAC and the Americas). In this role, you will analyse security events, investigate potential threats, validate and manage high-priority incidents, and execute decisive containment actions to minimise overall impact while escalating unresolved incidents to security engineering teams.

This person will monitor and remediate security incidents across on-prem, identity, and cloud-based environments for internal corporate infrastructure and enterprise client engagements. As the primary responder on shift during EMEA business hours, you should possess deep operational muscle memory, strong technical composure under pressure, and the initiative to challenge assumptions and propose continuous improvements. This is a remote role from either the UK, Ireland, or Poland.

Responsibilities

Lead triage, scoping, containment, and eradication for medium-to-high severity security incidents across endpoint, identity, SaaS, and cloud environments.
Perform deep-dive investigations, threat isolation, and query hunting leveraging CrowdStrike Falcon (Host Timeline, Real Time Response).
Investigate identity compromises, phishing campaigns, and suspicious account activities using Google Admin Console (Investigation Tool, Email Log Search, Token Auditing).
Analyse ingress edge telemetry, CDN traffic patterns, WAF events, and web server logs (including Cloudflare and Acquia application environments) to detect, trace, and mitigate web attacks, DDoS conditions, and botnet/scraping abuse.
Maintain and continuously update incident response plans and runbooks for efficient incident response, collaborating with engineering to automate containment workflows.
Coordinate cross-departmental remediation tasks and escalate unresolved incidents with clear technical root-cause analysis (RCA) aligned with MITRE ATT&CK.
Collaborate with content production for security awareness and mentorship.

About You

The essentials:

5+ years of direct experience in Security Operations (SOC), Incident Response, or similar hands-on technical operational roles.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science/Engineering/Information Security, or equivalent practical experience.
Deep operational experience utilising CrowdStrike (investigation workflows, Host Timeline, Real Time Response, and query hunting).
Proven experience leveraging Google Admin Console (Investigation Tool, Email Log Search, Token Auditing) for phishing, BEC, and identity investigations.
Hands-on experience with industry-leading security tools across EDR, SWG, SIEM, and MDM platforms.
Solid understanding of network protocols, traffic flow, and the OSI model.
Experience with log analysis, malware triage, and digital forensics.
Proven track record of operating autonomously during incidents with minimal supervision.
Practical experience leveraging AI tools, LLMs, or agentic workflows to assist analysis, scripting, or automation.
Working ITIL knowledge and functional familiarity with the MITRE ATT&CK framework.
Courteous, articulate, and educated in interpersonal delivery. Maintains a polite, respectful, and calm demeanor with internal teammates, leadership, and external clients even during incident bridges.
Ability to confidently and politely present findings to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we create content that informs, entertains and connects Canadians on multiple platforms. Our successes and accomplishments are driven by embodying and upholding values, which include creativity, integrity, inclusiveness and relevance.

Do you think you have the ability and drive to keep up with this exciting, ever-changing industry? Whether it be in front of the camera, on air, online or behind the scenes, you would be joining a team that thrives on making connections and telling stories that are important to Canadians.

Unposting Date

2026-11-19 11:59 PM

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technology and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

This is a hybrid role with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

Your Role

CBC/Radio-Canada is seeking a Lead Analyst, Continuous AI Risk Management Expert, to design, build and lead the enterprise-wide governance, security and continuous risk management program for artificial intelligence (covering both traditional AI and generative AI) across the Corporation.

In this role, you will design and deploy an enterprise AI risk assessment framework and conduct continuous evaluations of AI systems throughout the AI life cycle (from design to production). You will collaborate closely with data protection analysts, as well as the legal, compliance and enterprise architecture teams, to identify, measure and mitigate cybersecurity risks associated with AI technologies.

This position can be based in Montreal or Toronto.

What’s In It For You

Challenges. We spend our days solving problems of all kinds. Media files are highly nuanced and incredibly complicated; updating, installing and supporting technologies that are organization-wide and that impact broadcasting content is a time-sensitive, complex technical feat. And that’s just the beginning. You’ll be working with leading-edge data management, cloud, IP broadcasting, AI, security and reliability technologies.

As Lead Analyst, You Will

Design and deploy the AI risk assessment framework: Develop, formalize and implement a standardized risk assessment methodology tailored to AI systems, including ethical impact matrices, model criticality criteria, bias analysis, algorithmic vulnerability assessments and data exposure risks.
Support enterprise AI governance architecture: Collaborate closely with architecture teams and governance committees to design, integrate and evolve the security foundation for AI technologies across the Corporation.
Maintain the AI inventory and classification: Build and manage a centralized registry of all AI systems, models (internal, SaaS, open-source) and AI agents deployed across the organization, classified by risk level.
Conduct continuous model risk assessments: Perform technical risk evaluations on new AI use cases, analyzing training data security, prompt/query confidentiality, algorithmic bias and intellectual property risks.
Perform AI security testing: Define and execute specialized security and adversarial testing for AI and large language models (LLMs).
Assess third-party AI and SaaS solutions: Partner with the Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) Analyst to evaluate the security posture, privacy controls and model-training policies of external vendors. Provide specialized AI expertise to analyze contractual data-use terms (e.g., ensuring corporate data is not used for model training), evaluate SaaS API security and verify privacy guarantees in third-party environments.
Manage the AI risk register: Document, maintain and map AI-specific model vulnerabilities, technical debt and approved exceptions in the risk register.
Assess program maturity: Conduct periodic evaluations of AI governance maturity, developing dashboards and tracking key performance indicators (KPIs) and key risk indicators (KRIs) for executive and governance committees.
Maintain industry expertise: Stay current on information security best practices and industry trends.

What You Bring

University degree in computer science, IT or information security.
Minimum five years' applied experience in IT security, data governance or technology risk management.
Demonstrated experience in designing or implementing risk assessment methodologies and evaluating AI models.
Proven ability to translate complex AI concepts into structured risk frameworks for project teams, with a deep understanding of AI architectures and AI-specific attack vectors.
Extensive knowledge of security technology and risk assessment methodologies, policies and processes.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to translate complex technical concepts for non-technical decision-makers (e.g., governance committees, business units, legal teams).
Excellent analytical, evaluative and problem-solving abilities.
Experience with compliance programs as well as their technical and security requirements.
Technical expertise across key domains:
Standards and Frameworks: Strong command of industry standards such as ISO/IEC 27001, 27002, 27005, NIST SP 800-53 / 800-161, COBIT and ITIL.
Cloud and Web Architecture Security: Solid understanding of web infrastructure and cloud environment security.
Network and Security Technologies: Thorough understanding of network architectures (LAN/WAN, routers), network security technologies (firewalls, IDS/IPS, DNS, web filtering) and cryptographic principles (encryption at rest and in transit).
Architecture and Data Security: Working knowledge of database architecture concepts and secure software development best practices.
Operational Resilience and Physical Security: Solid understanding of business continuity and disaster recovery planning (BCP/DRP), operational resilience and physical security controls.

Relevant professional security certifications a definite asset (e.g., CISSP, CRISC, CBCP, CISA, CISM or equivalent).
Bilingualism (English and French) essential.

Summary

Gibson Dunn is a leading global law firm, advising clients on significant transactions and disputes. Our exceptional teams craft and deploy creative legal strategies that are meticulously tailored to every matter, however complex or high-stakes. The firm’s work is distinguished by a unique combination of precision and vision.

Based in Los Angeles, Palo Alto, San Francisco, Orange County, Houston, Dallas or Denver, the Market Intelligence Manager will be responsible for owning a portfolio of recurring intelligence products and ad hoc research projects from intake through delivery.

The Market Intelligence team sits within the Marketing / Client Development department and produces the research that drives the firm’s business development: background reports on people and companies, deal and litigation analytics, recurring monitoring reports and real-time opportunity alerts for partners and practice group leaders worldwide.

This is a project-management and individual-contributor role rather than a people-management role: the Manager scopes requests, sets timelines, coordinates inputs from colleagues and subscription platforms, applies quality control, and delivers finished, partner-ready work product. The role requires working fluency in either corporate/transactional practice or litigation and disputes, and the ability to learn the other.

This role reports to the Sr. Manager, Market Intelligence.

Responsibilities Include

Project and Product Ownership

Own assigned recurring intelligence products end to end: define scope, maintain the production schedule, manage data sources and templates, and ensure on-time, consistent delivery.
Scope and prioritize incoming research requests; confirm the question being asked, agree deadlines and format with the requesting attorney, and manage expectations when requests compete.
Coordinate multi-part projects that draw on several colleagues, databases or offices, tracking progress and consolidating inputs into a single deliverable.
Serve as primary Market Intelligence contact for designated practice groups or business development leads, building an understanding of their priorities and target clients.
Maintain and improve the team’s templates, house style, and documentation so that recurring products can be reproduced consistently.

Research and Intelligence Requests

Background intelligence on people: compile and synthesize public-record, news and subscription-database findings; use AI (artificial intelligence) tools to draft first-pass profiles and surface patterns across large volumes of material.
Company intelligence reports: cover corporate, financial and litigation activity; use AI to summarize filings, dockets, news and long-form documents into decision-ready narratives.
Deal exports: run and refine screens in Mergermarket, PitchBook, LSEG Workspace (formerly Refinitiv), Preqin and Bloomberg, including each platform’s AI-enabled features and connected tools, and translate raw exports into formatted deliverables.
Litigation analytics: export and interpret analytics from Bloomberg Law and Lex Machina (judge, counsel, timing and outcome trends), and narrate the results for non-specialist audiences.
News monitoring: search Law360, Law.com, Bloomberg Law and open web sources, using AI-assisted monitoring and summarization to keep recurring alerts and daily digests current.
Ad hoc research: apply sound judgment about when AI is appropriate and when primary-source review is required.

Practice-Specific Reports and Alerts

Daily report on stocks that have fallen below a defined threshold (requires a Bloomberg Anywhere license).
Daily report on securities litigation cases of possible interest.
News alerts: monitor and distribute business development triggers to partners in real time, including new general counsel appointments, executive and other senior personnel changes, and significant filings.
International arbitration weekly round-up: compile a weekly digest of international arbitration news, awards and enforcement developments for the practice group.
IPO (initial public offering) candidate report identifying companies in later-stage funding rounds that may be preparing to go public.
Other opportunity-spotting reports (for example, the Spain Target Tracker and the Arbitral Enforcement Report), and development of new ones as practice needs emerge.

AI Enablement

Design, test and refine prompts, skills and repeatable AI workflows for recurring research products, including client dossiers, target-list matching, daily monitoring reports and formatted fact sheets.
Apply consistent quality control to AI output: confirm citations against primary sources, flag hallucinated or stale information, and escalate where AI-generated analysis is not appropriate for client-facing use.

Job Information

Job Title: Research and Program Analyst & Data and Research Analyst

Job Requisition ID: 88893

Ministry: Assisted Living and Social Services

Hours of Work: 36.25 hours per week

Closing Date: November 25, 2026

Salary: $3,148.20 - $4,126.82 bi-weekly ($82,168 - $107,710/year)

The Alberta Public Service works to build a stronger province for current and future generations. We make a difference in the lives of Albertans through rewarding career opportunities.

The Ministry of Assisted Living and Social Services leads housing, assisted living and continuing care, seniors, income, employment and homelessness supports, disability services, and other social-based programs. For more information about ALSS, visit our website: Assisted Living and Social Services .

Working within the Research & Analytics Unit of the Housing Division, you will contribute to the development of analytical products and reporting processes that support accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement across housing programs and initiatives. Through your expertise in data management and analysis, you will help provide decision-makers with the information they need to improve outcomes for Albertans.

The Housing Division is hiring for two permanent positions in its Research Unit.

Research and Program Analyst

Are you an experienced policy and program analyst who can turn complex and sometimes conflicting evidence into practical advice? The Housing Division is seeking a Research and Program Analyst to lead research and evaluation work, develop evidence-based policy and program options, examine business processes and housing application approaches, and identify emerging housing issues and research priorities.

Data and Research Analyst

Do you enjoy finding reliable numbers when a decision can’t wait? You’ll answer time-sensitive questions about housing programs and finances, build budgeting and forecasting tools for other teams, and pursue deeper questions between requests.

Role Responsibilities

Research and Program Analyst

Reporting to the Manager, Data & Research, the Research and Program Analyst provides independent research, evaluation and practical advice to help the Housing Division resolve policy, program and business problems. Working in the Research Unit of the Policy, Planning and Intergovernmental Branch, the position develops evidence-based options and recommendations that reflect government priorities, operational realities, applicant experiences and the perspectives of housing delivery partners.

Key Responsibilities Include:

Policy and program research and advice

Clarify policy, program and business problems, decision requirements, intended outcomes, constraints, research scope and timelines with requesting areas.
Examine policies, program information, administrative and financial evidence, stakeholder perspectives and approaches used in other jurisdictions.
Develop and compare feasible options, assessing benefits, costs, operational implications, risks and unintended consequences for applicants, delivery partners and the ministry.
Prepare clear recommendations, reports and briefing materials that explain the evidence, trade-offs, limitations and decisions required.

Program evaluation

Lead assigned housing program evaluations by establishing evaluation questions, scope, work plans and deliverables with program areas and the Manager, Data & Research.
Develop evaluation frameworks that connect program objectives, activities and intended outcomes, and identify appropriate indicators, evidence sources and methods.
Coordinate evidence gathering through document review, administrative information, interviews and other appropriate methods.
Assess findings against program objectives and evaluation criteria, identify data gaps and methodological limitations, and develop actionable recommendations.

Business process and service-design analysis

Examine applicant, Housing Management Body and ministry staff experiences to identify barriers, duplicated effort, inconsistent practices and unmet business needs.
Map process steps, information requirements and decision points, and distinguish essential requirements from practices that can be reconsidered.
Research and recommend a standardized housing application approach that balances consistent information with accessibility, applicant effort and Housing Management Body capacity.
Develop and compare proposed process designs, business requirements or conceptual application formats and obtain user and specialist feedback.

Emerging issues and research priorities

Maintain awareness of government priorities, ministry direction, policy developments and emerging housing issues.
Build working relationships with program staff and housing delivery partners to understand front-line conditions and concerns.
Compare operational accounts and applicant experiences with quantitative findings to identify patterns, conflicting explanations and evidence gaps.
Maintain and recommend a prioritized set of emerging research questions for the Housing Division.

The Job Description is provided for further details on this position.

Data and Research Analyst

Reporting to the Manager, Data & Research, you’ll take responsibility for requests from the first conversation through to the answer. You’ll work with program and policy teams to understand the decision they face and deliver analysis they can use.

Rapid analysis and advice

Clarify the decision, the numbers needed and the deadline. Find suitable program and financial data, check their quality and choose a method that fits the question.
Estimate the effects of a proposed change. For example, model how a change to an income threshold could affect housing providers’ revenue. Explain the range of estimates and the assumptions that matter most.
Brief the requesting team on what the evidence supports, where it is uncertain and what that means for the decision.

Focused research

Between requests, identify questions that merit closer analysis. Investigate unexpected patterns and test alternative explanations.
Bring forward findings that challenge an assumption or change how a program team understands an issue.

Program performance measurement

Develop indicators with program teams that reflect the outcomes they need to understand. Agree on definitions and identify reliable data sources.
Track results over time, investigate changes and flag data limitations that affect how teams should interpret the measures.

The Job Description is provided for further details on this position.

APS Competencies

Competencies are behaviors that are essential to reach our goals in serving Albertans. We encourage you to have an in depth understanding of the competencies that are required for this opportunity and to be prepared to demonstrate them during the recruitment process.

Creative Problem Solving: Defines complex and ambiguous problems, tests assumptions, reconciles conflicting evidence and develops practical options where no single established answer exists.
Systems Thinking: Considers how policy choices, program objectives, business processes, applicant experiences, delivery partner capacity and information requirements affect one another and the broader housing system.
Agility: Adjusts analysis, research and evaluation plans when priorities, timelines or available evidence change, explains implications and identifies practical alternatives.
Drive for Results: Takes ownership of analytical requests, research and evaluation assignments from scoping through recommendations, resolves obstacles, raises risks early and delivers accurate, decision-ready advice.
Build Collaborative Environments: Creates space for program staff, quantitative analysts, subject-matter experts and housing delivery partners to contribute different perspectives while remaining accountable for independent analysis and recommendations.

Qualifications

Research and Program Analyst

University graduation in Public Administration, Public Policy, Political Science, Social Sciences, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field, plus 4 years of progressively responsible related experience; or equivalent as described below.

Equivalency: Directly related education or experience considered on the basis of:

1 year of education for 1 year of experience; or
1 year of experience for 1 year of education.

The Following Experience Is Required:

Conducting independent policy and program research and developing evidence-based options and recommendations for decision-makers.
Leading or conducting program evaluations, including developing evaluation questions or frameworks, selecting methods, assessing findings and preparing actionable recommendations.
Analyzing complex quantitative and qualitative evidence, testing assumptions, reconciling conflicting information and clearly explaining limitations or uncertainty.
Examining business processes, service design or program administration and recommending practical improvements.
Managing research or evaluation projects, including scope, work plans, timelines, stakeholder input and deliverables.
Strong Excel skills and an understanding of how evidence and advice inform government decisions.

The Following Experience Is Considered An Asset:

Understanding housing policy, housing programs, social policy or programs delivered through third-party or community-based partners.
Developing or assessing business requirements, standardized application approaches, forms or service processes. Using administrative, financial and program data in a government policy or evaluation environment.

Data and Research Analyst

University graduation in Economics, Business, Data Analytics, Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science or a related field, plus four years of progressively responsible related experience. The same one-for-one education and experience equivalencies apply to this position.

The Following Experience Is Required:

Independently turning a time-sensitive request into an analytical question, finding suitable data and checking its quality before reporting results.
Strong Excel skills, including modelling scenarios or forecasts. Experience preparing and analyzing data in Python, R, SAS or a comparable analytical environment.
Developing tools or repeatable reports for other users, documenting how they work and helping users interpret the results.
Explaining findings, assumptions and limitations to colleagues who need to make a decision.

The Following Experience Is Considered An Asset:

Experience with Power BI or a similar visualization tool, or with developing measures to track program outcomes over time.

Hours of work are 08:15 AM to 04:30 PM, Monday to Friday working 36.25 hours per week. You must be living in or be willing to relocate to work in Edmonton.

Location: 44 Capital Boulevard, 10044 - 108 Street, Edmonton, Alberta, T5J3S7.

Experience partnering across departments (such as Sales, Operations, and Marketing) to improve tools or workflows preferred.

Generous paid time off

With all of the information available today, it takes a skilled all-source analyst to know how to find and interpret the best data to give their clients the right answers. With the critical decisions made in our government and military every day, we need an intelligence analyst like you to do just that. As an all-source analyst, you use your specialized functional experience and your attention to detail to conduct all-source analytic production on foreign defense industrial programs, infrastructure, and capabilities supporting a foreign country’s ability to develop, equip, sustain, and employ its military forces across basic, strategic, and military industrial sectors.

As an All-Source Analyst on our team, you’ll help your client by providing intelligence production and briefing support to address dynamic intelligence requirements. Using your comprehensive understanding of all-source analytic tradecraft, production cycles, publication standards, community writing styles, and formats, you’ll produce strategic-level assessments and products that address the research, development, acquisition, test, evaluation and production of foreign weapon systems and equipment. As an authority on your topic, your client will look to you for comprehensive production, often under pressure.

This is a chance to grow your expertise and broaden your skillset in areas like analysis, writing, and communication. You’ll share your expertise with other analysts through leadership and mentoring. We focus on growing as a team to deliver the best support to our customers, so you’ll have resources to learn new skills and tools. Join us as we provide the right information at the right time to support the critical needs of our warfighters and nation’s leaders.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

Knowledge of IC and Combatant Command environments
Ability to develop high-quality deliverables tailored to senior policymakers or defense stakeholders, including complex written products and formal or informal briefings
TS/SCI clearance
Bachelor's degree and 3+ years of experience in all-source analysis, or 7+ years of experience in all-source analysis in lieu of a degree

Knowledge of ICD 203 and 206 analytic tradecraft standards

The Senior Data Analyst – Governance reports to the Associate Director, Governance and is responsible for building and maintaining enterprise-wide Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) that monitor Business Continuity Risk and Operational Resilience exposure. The role combines data analytics, including developing methodologies, automated dashboards, and visualizations, with data engineering, including sourcing, integrating, and validating enterprise data and enforcing data quality controls. The analyst works with the Associate Director, Platform Business Continuity Management (BCM) teams, and data owners turn business requirements into technical solutions and to support regulatory compliance. What will you do?

Support the design and implementation of enterprise-wide KRI/KPI frameworks, including measurement methodologies, calculation specifications, and data collection processes.

:

The Business Continuity & Resilience Program Manager is responsible for leading the implementation, enablement, and continuous improvement of the company’s business continuity management (BCM) program. Operating as a program leader and internal consultant, this role partners across business and technology teams to drive alignment, consistency, and adoption of continuity practices. Program Leadership & Execution

A systems thinker who can connect risk, operations, and strategy.
Highly organized, analytical, and focused on continuous improvement.
An effective communicator who can engage both operational teams and senior stakeholders.
Able to translate business continuity concepts and processes to enable business needs and requirements.
Able to function as a consultant to business and technology management regarding business continuity matters.
Experienced working with international business entities.

YOU HAVE

7-10 years of experience in business continuity, disaster recovery, crisis management, resilience or related disciplines.
Experience leading or supporting enterprise programs, including process design and implementation
Strong background in process development, governance frameworks, and program management

University Overview

The University of Pennsylvania, the largest private employer in Philadelphia, is a world-renowned leader in education, research, and innovation. This historic, Ivy League school consistently ranks among the top 10 universities in the annual U.S. News & World Report survey. Penn has 12 highly-regarded schools that provide opportunities for undergraduate, graduate and continuing education, all influenced by Penn’s distinctive interdisciplinary approach to scholarship and learning. As an employer Penn has been ranked nationally on many occasions with the most recent award from Forbes who named Penn one of America’s Best Large Employers in 2023.

Penn offers a unique working environment within the city of Philadelphia. The University is situated on a beautiful urban campus, with easy access to a range of educational, cultural, and recreational activities. With its historical significance and landmarks, lively cultural offerings, and wide variety of atmospheres, Philadelphia is the perfect place to call home for work and play.

The University offers a competitive benefits package that includes excellent healthcare and tuition benefits for employees and their families, generous retirement benefits, a wide variety of professional development opportunities, supportive work and family benefits, a wealth of health and wellness programs and resources, and much more.

Posted Job Title

Practice Based Research Network (PBRN) Data Analyst

Job Profile Title

Biostatistician

Job Description Summary

The Primary Care Practice-Based Research Network (PBRN) Data Analyst will provide data management and analytic support for research and programmatic activities conducted through the Practice-Based Research Network (PBRN). Reporting to the PBRN Manager and working closely with PBRN leadership, investigators, research staff, clinicians, and health system data partners, the Data Analyst will support the acquisition, management, analysis, visualization, and interpretation of survey, electronic health record (EHR), and other healthcare data.

The Data Analyst will contribute across the research lifecycle, including developing analytic datasets, conducting data quality assessments, performing statistical analyses, preparing data visualizations and reports, and supporting interpretation and dissemination of findings. A key component of the position will be ongoing training and professional development in Penn Medicine-specific data systems, with the goal of developing increasing expertise and independence in accessing, querying, managing, and analyzing EHR data to support practice-based research.

Job Description

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:

Data Management and Quality Assurance
Develop, maintain, clean, and document research and operational datasets derived from surveys, EHRs, and other healthcare data sources.
Perform data validation, quality assurance, and routine audits to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and integrity of PBRN data.
Develop reproducible processes for data cleaning, transformation, linkage, and preparation for analysis.
Maintain data dictionaries, analytic documentation, and other resources necessary to support reproducible research.
Work with research, clinical, informatics, and IT partners to identify and resolve data quality and data management issues.

Statistical Analysis and Data Visualization
Conduct descriptive and inferential statistical analyses to support PBRN research, program evaluation, and network activities.
Work with investigators and PBRN leadership to translate research questions into appropriate analytic approaches.
Develop tables, figures, dashboards, and other data visualizations that effectively communicate findings to research, clinical, operational, and community audiences.
Assist with interpretation of findings and preparation of analytic results for presentations, reports, abstracts, manuscripts, and grant applications.
Provide analytic consultation and support to PBRN investigators and project teams within the scope of the position.
Electronic Health Record Data and Clinical Informatics
Support acquisition, management, and analysis of EHR data for PBRN research and network activities.
Work collaboratively with health system data and informatics teams to develop and validate data queries and understand the structure, availability, limitations, and appropriate use of clinical data.
Develop increasing expertise in querying relational healthcare databases and extracting data needed for study feasibility, cohort identification, research analyses, and evaluation of clinical interventions.
Participate in ongoing training in Penn Medicine-specific EHR, data warehouse, and research data systems, with the expectation of progressively developing greater independence in EHR data access and analysis.
Experience with EHR data extraction, SQL queries, or Epic data environments is desirable but not required at the time of hire.
Research and PBRN Collaboration
Collaborate with investigators, clinicians, research coordinators, PBRN leadership, and other members of multidisciplinary research teams.
Assist teams in assessing the availability, quality, and limitations of data relevant to proposed research questions.

Diversity is one of our biggest strengths. Our differences are what make us distinct. We respect each other and believe in equal opportunities for all.

new_jobs.title: Data Analyst I (SB)
new_jobs.description:
Overview

Goldbelt Professional Services specializes in providing expert resources for Public Health missions including scientific, technical, and administrative support from junior staff to high-level subject matter experts. Research and data driven, Goldbelt Professional Services’ experts create solutions customized to the client’s needs.

Summary:

Goldbelt Professional Services is seeking a Data Analyst I to provide NHSN Dialysis Event Prevention and surveillance training support within the Surveillance Branch (SB).

Responsibilities

Essential Job Functions:

Provide direct user support guidance for the NHSN Dialysis Event module from a user perspective.
Conduct user outreach and education and provide consultation/technical assistance to dialysis provider groups, quality improvement organizations, and health departments.
Analyze the NHSN system's daily function and develop system modifications to improve data quality; track modifications.
Update surveillance forms, instructions, and protocols with improvement recommendations.
Develop data validation projects to evaluate and improve quality.
Work with Division SMEs to enhance usability of NHSN surveillance data for prevention efforts.
Manage reports, data file exchanges, and agreements between CDC and partner organizations.
Review user inquiries related to NHSN and CMS quality incentive programs and prepare response documents.
Handle inquiries, perform enrollment, and support correct application of CDC HAI definitions and data entry. Expected volume is 212 per month (range 122-415).
Identify user/system issues requiring modification; contribute to development and prioritization of modifications.
Develop NHSN modules and electronic reporting mechanisms; communicate with users to improve interface and group functions.
Prepare and present educational trainings (20-30 annually) about NHSN.
Write and review training/educational documents and outreach messages.
Contribute subject matter support for meeting planning related to NHSN, the Coalition, and dialysis safety.
Create draft CDC communication materials promoting HAI prevention strategies.
Write/review content for the CDC Dialysis Safety webpage.
Perform data management, cleaning, and quality assessment analyses.
Perform NHSN data analyses for CMS quality incentive programs and create user reports.
Advocate with partners to increase participation in ESRD Network, NCC, and other CMS HAI prevention activities.
Develop and promote CDC infection prevention and surveillance resources.
Review and develop website materials and communications related to infection prevention, surveillance, and response.
Participate during CDC response activities and training exercises under direction of the DHQP Team Lead; duties include staffing the EOC desk to help support CDC's mission.

Qualifications

Necessary Skills and Knowledge:

Knowledge of the principles, concepts, methods, and techniques of public health research and evaluation to analyze, evaluate, and provide expert advice and consultation.
Knowledge of the principles, methods, applications, and state-of-the-art technology in the position's scientific area of responsibility to provide direction and guidance on critical and complex issues.
Ability to communicate orally and in writing to make clear, convincing presentations.
Knowledge of the rules, procedures, and principles that govern intramural and extramural program development, monitoring, and evaluation.
Highly proficient in using Microsoft Office Tools (Word, Excel, Access, PowerPoint, Teams, and SharePoint).
Excellent judgment and decision-making; capable of working independently with ability to multitask successfully.
Demonstrate excellent written and verbal communication in interpersonal exchanges.
Highly organized with great attention to detail.

Minimum Qualifications:

1 - 2 years of experience providing public health data analysis and manipulating, cleaning, and reporting data using a variety of statistical functions.
Highly proficient in using various statistical software (SAS, R, Python, etc.)
Knowledge of data management systems and application of data management software.
Previous experience working with the government procedures and guidelines.
Ability to obtain and maintain CDC Public Trust Clearance.

Preferred Qualifications:

Master’s degree in Statistics, Data Science, Public Health, or related field.
3 - 5 years of experience providing public health data analysis and manipulating, cleaning, and reporting data using a variety of statistical functions.
Prior experience working with the CDC is highly desired to understand the culture and environment.

Pay And Benefits

The salary range for this position is $80,000.00 to $90,000.00 annually.

At Goldbelt, we value and reward our team's dedication and hard work. We provide a competitive base salary commensurate with your qualifications and experience. As an employee, you'll enjoy a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k) plan with company matching, tax-deferred savings options, supplementary benefits, paid time off, and professional development opportunities.

new_jobs.description:
About The Company

DiDi Global Inc. is the world’s leading mobility technology platform. It offers a wide range of app-based services across markets including Asia-Pacific, Latin America and Africa, including ride hailing, taxi hailing, chauffeur, hitch and other forms of shared mobility as well as auto solutions, food delivery, intra-city freight, and financial services.

DiDi provides car owners, drivers, and delivery partners with flexible work and income opportunities. It is committed to collaborating with policymakers, the taxi industry, the automobile industry and the communities to solve the world’s transportation, environmental and employment challenges through the use of AI technology and localized smart transportation innovations. DiDi strives to create better life experiences and greater social value, by building a safe, inclusive and sustainable transportation and local services ecosystem for cities of the future.

For more information, please visit: www.didiglobal.com/news

About The Team/role

The ANZ Marketplace team owns the health of our ride-hailing marketplace across Australia and New Zealand — spanning trading efficiency, rider and driver experience, and risk & anti-fraud strategy. We work close to the business: diagnosing what's driving our core metrics, designing strategies from the ground up, and validating them in the real world. This role sits at the intersection of business and operations, with plenty of room to shape decisions that directly affect the experience of riders and drivers.

In this role, you'll be...

Develop a deep understanding of our ride-hailing marketplace — identify problems, get to the root cause behind movements in core business metrics (trading efficiency, rider/driver experience, etc.), and deliver optimisation recommendations backed by sound business judgement
Break down business situations in rider experience and operations (cancellation fees, cleaning fees, routing & toll disputes, driver misconduct, etc.), turning vague business phenomena into clear, actionable problems
Use data (data pulling, metric monitoring, and experiment validation where needed) to support business decisions, judge whether strategies are effective, and drive iteration
Capture analytical conclusions and business methodology into the team's ops tracker / knowledge base, improving how efficiently the team understands the business
Collaborate with Product, Operations, Risk and other cross-functional teams to drive project delivery across the Beijing and ANZ time zones

We're eager to be in touch because you have...

Bachelor's degree or above; discipline open, with a quantitative background (statistics, mathematics, actuarial studies, computer science, economics, engineering etc.) preferred
1–3 years of experience in operations / business analysis / strategy (outstanding new or recent graduates will also be considered)
Strong business understanding and logical judgement — able to independently break down ambiguous requirements into a clear analytical framework and reach conclusions with real commercial sense
Strong learner, highly proactive, able to make progress even when information is incomplete
Good written and verbal communication in both English and Chinese, comfortable collaborating across cross-functional teams

You'll love working at DiDi because...

We create user value

We strive to always create valuable experiences for our users in everything we do. Our focus is to always innovate new experiences that are safe, pleasant and efficient.

We are data-driven

We are strong believers in making informed decisions, that’s why we are data-driven. We can better navigate the business landscape strategically by analyzing valuable metrics.

Win-win Collaboration

Success is a team sport. When we work to help our partners and colleagues win, we win, too. While keeping everyone's best interest at heart, we communicate with candor and execute with excellence in all we do.

We believe in integrity

Integrity is at the very core of our business. We are people who always want to do the right thing. Our intentions are sincere, we speak our minds and listen to each other.

Growth

We always strive to do better. That means venturing beyond our comfort zones, learning from our mistakes, and helping each other grow.

Diversity and Inclusion

Diversity is one of our biggest strengths. Our differences are what make us distinct. We respect each other and believe in equal opportunities for all.

We are committed to building inclusive and diverse teams

At DiDi, we believe that our differences are our biggest source of strength. That’s why we are committed to promoting equal opportunities to all candidates and employees as an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Employment and advancement decisions at DiDi are always made based on the needs of the position and the qualifications of the candidate. We do not discriminate against any employee or applicant based on their gender, age, sexual orientation, nationality, marital status, pregnancy/maternity, disability, race, religion and beliefs, or any other status protected by applicable laws wherever we operate.

We are committed to building inclusive and diverse teams, and a workplace that is free from discrimination and harassment, because that’s how we create better products and services, make better decisions and better serve the communities we’re a part of.
